#1715. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1714. Top Gun, tears, thrills and the future script: Cardinale the leading actor in rollercoaster visit

When he touched down in Italy before the Udinese game, not even Gerry Cardinale himself will have foreseen the whirlwind week that followed.

The visit of the Milan owner was known about ahead of time, as were his motivations. Cardinale not only wanted to demonstrate his closeness to the team in a very important moment, but he also had a lot of off-field issues to tackle too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He would end up staying in the country for one week, something that has not been common. This is a different version of the RedBird Capital founder that we are seeing though, one that seems more hands-on than ever when it comes to steering the ship.

Or rather, in this case, it was a bit of a rollercoaster that he was at the front of. It started with a climb, continued with a steep drop, and then came the ascent which ultimately led into take-off on his flight back to America.

Things started quite well for Cardinale in his latest visit, as Milan went away to Udinese and won 2-0 thanks to goals from Christian Pulisic and Omari Hutchinson, bouncing back well from the defeat in Bournemouth a few nights prior.

Attention then shifted to the midweek meeting with a resurgent Bologna side at San Siro, and things did not go as well. Alphadjo Cisse’s brace was ultimately outshone by Samuel Mbangula’s hat-trick, as the Rossoblu scored three unanswered second-half goals to win 4-2.

It was a crash back down to earth, and a further reminder that this team remains very much a work in progress, with obvious limitations and shortcomings that can be exploited in quite a ruthless way. With the loss, Milan moved seven points off the leaders Inter and Lazio.

A few days ago, after the win in Udine, Cardinale had praised both the team and Ruben Amorim in a post-match interview. After the Bologna game, the owner not only didn’t speak, but left the stadium looking rather glum to say the least.

Sometimes, though, the curses can be a blessing too. Perhaps this was a necessary reminder for everyone – from Cardinale down to the players – that there is no shortcut with this project, and that there will be growing pains.

It cannot be argued though that it set a rather gloomy backdrop to everything that would come in the next few days, which makes what actually happened all the more remarkable.

The big day finally arrived on Thursday, just 24 hours after the Bologna match: Milan and Inter unveiled the renderings of their new stadium, along with design studios Foster+Partners and Manica.

The timing of the event – which took place at the Sforzesco in the city centre – felt deliberate. Just two days before the derby, Milan and Inter got together to release the first images of how the new stadium will look.

Some details had been known for some time about the specifics of the project, but visualising it is another thing. Moreover, they dropped the bombshell before hand that a day one naming rights partner had been found: Generali, thus making it the Generali Stadium.

❗ OFFICIAL: How #ACMilan and Inter's new home the 'Generali Stadium' will look.

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) October 29, 2026

Leaving aside any subjective thoughts on the design, it was a very proud moment for Cardinale. The American had made no secret of his desire to construct a new home for the two clubs, and he shed some light on things in an interview with CBS.

“You know, when we bought the club four years ago, I started working on this right away. And part of what we’re trying to do here is bring the best of America to Italian soccer, and specifically to AC Milan.

“It’s extraordinary: most people didn’t think we could accomplish all this, or even get to this point. Not only did we announce the stadium this week, but we also announced the largest naming rights deal in history. I think it’s a wonderful thing for Italian soccer.

“The message to everyone is that we’re coming back. Italian soccer truly deserves to be at the top again, and we’ll do everything we can through AC Milan to make that happen.”

Something about the build-up to the derby, right up until kick-off, felt different. It seemed as though there was a conscious decision to try and create a connection with the past, something that Cardinale himself appeared to lead.

For example, Sky reported that Cardinale invited about 60 people to a dinner the night before the game. It wasn’t just an opportunity to catch up, but also for the American to explain what he has planned for Milan, seeking the support of some club legends.

The likes of Adriano Galliani, Ricardo Kaka and the Serie A president Simonelli attended the dinner. Other notable Milan legends present were Marcel Desailly, Serginho, Cristian Brocchi, Mathieu Flamini, Mauro Tassotti, Filippo Galli and Daniele Massaro.

At the Milan Store, racks of shirts adorned printing with names like Gattuso, Nesta, Seedorf, Inzaghi, Pirlo, Ambrosini, Kaka and even Maldini. The tag line behind the campaign was to ‘celebrate the heroes of Athens’, but again it felt like constructed timing.

Going back to that CBS interview, the bold proclamations that Cardinale made on the broadcast certainly turned some heads.

“I remember George Steinbrenner telling me about twenty years ago, ‘Don’t get too emotionally involved in all this, don’t go into the locker room, don’t do those things’. But in this case, I got emotionally involved,” he said.

“For me, it became a personal issue. And I don’t know what it is: maybe it’s just that… look around, listen. This means so much to the people of Milan, it has a huge impact on them, and I feel a huge responsibility.

“AC Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there. This will probably be one of the greatest things I’ll do in my career.”

Speaking of that link with the past, Kaka was presented with a trophy before kick-off to mark his induction into the Rossoneri Hall of Fame. It was a moment filled with emotion for all the fans present who chanted his name, while the Brazilian couldn’t hold back the tears as a montage video played on the screen.

Those words might just have fallen very flat had Milan not delivered on the field, but they did. No doubt fired up by the emotionally-charged atmosphere inside the stadium, Gerry Cardinale got to watch on as his players delivered a show.

Diego Moreira – the man he reportedly pushed to sign personally for €51m – was the start of the show. He got two assists from Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot, two of his other favourites, before bending in a free-kick of his own. It was enough to blow the champions away.

Just 72 hours earlier, Cardinale had trudged through the mixed zone barely able to make eye contact with reporters after seeing his team implode against (at the time) bottom-half Bologna. On Halloween night, he had the smile of a child who had just scooped all the candy.

Speaking to QSVS, he got emotional: “What did you think of the boys? Every three days playing a game, going through the injuries, we get our full team back, and look at those guys. Those guys are winners. It brings tears to my eyes, it’s great right? The best night, and we’re going to build on this.”

🥲 “Look at those guys… it brings tears to my eyes.”

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 1, 2026

All of the pre-match hype, those ballsy interviews speaking of a desire to return to greatness, bringing legends back to invoke the nostalgia… it was a very risky move in hindsight. It could have backfired with a defeat, but the team delivered and gave everyone connected to the club immense pride.

So, within the space of four days and 180 minutes of football, Cardinale had witnessed both the floor and the ceiling of this team. The next mission – one he appears to be well aware of – is to bring the baseline up towards the obvious high potential Amorim’s group has.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport before the Inter game, the 59-year-old admitted that the squad is far from finished in his eyes, and that some further work is needed to try and get it up to the level required. He also invoked Top Gun to explain his bond with Amorim.

“We need to continue improving the squad because in the summer I wasn’t able to do everything I wanted. We’re rebuilding the team, and while I like the new arrivals, the ones who stayed, and the names I got rid of, it will probably take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.

“We’re only a quarter of the way there, and the priority is to build a team that can deal with injuries. If you’re competing in European competitions and playing… Amorim Ball, which is high-tempo football, with quick transitions, where everyone runs between 9 and 11km per game, you have to rotate them.

“That’s why we’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic in the January transfer market, and I’ll continue to strengthen our bench. My style is to move decisively and quickly.

“What matters to me is getting what we want, players… that are Milan-worthy. I won’t waste money, but when I set my mind on signing a player, I do everything I can to succeed.”

The first big step will be to welcome a very important jigsaw piece to complete the management puzzle: Markus Krösche. The past few days also seemed to serve to iron out the remaining details to reach an agreement with the German, who will become the new Head of Football.

You may wish to remain sceptical, and that is absolutely warranted, but for the first time in a while there does seem to be the semblance of a path out of the rut. A more active owner, a talented squad with room to improve, a coach being backed, a key director incoming and a new stadium on the way.

Oh, and of course the bragging rights, which are heading back across the Atlantic Ocean with Cardinale while he no doubt draws up the itinerary for his next visit.

#1713. Real Madrid's Nico Paz decision in focus after Como record

By Naim Beneddra | 05 Nov 2026 18:54

Real Madrid's decision to allow Nico Paz to remain at Como for another season has come under renewed scrutiny after the Argentine midfielder inspired another remarkable Champions League performance.

The 22-year-old scored once and provided two assists as Cesc Fabregas's side demolished Lens 9-1 on Wednesday evening, equalling the biggest winning margin in Champions League history and setting a new record for the competition's largest away victory.

Paz has now registered three goals and five assists in just four Champions League appearances this season, making him the competition's most productive player in terms of direct goal involvements.

His extraordinary form is particularly significant for Real Madrid, who agreed to let the midfielder continue his development in Italy during the summer but retained the right to bring him back in 2027.

With Como emerging as one of Europe's most exciting attacking teams, the decision to leave Paz under Fabregas's guidance is attracting fresh attention.

8 - Nico Paz leads all players for goal involvements in the @ChampionsLeague this season (3 goals, 5 assists). Only Raúl in 2002-03 and Neymar in 2016-17 have ever had more assists in their first four appearances of a single edition (6 each). Magic. https://t.co/SpSk28QrwH

Como's astonishing victory in France featured a hat-trick from Anastasios Douvikas, but Paz once again demonstrated why he has become the creative heartbeat of Fabregas's team.

The Argentina international scored Como's third goal in the 40th minute, arriving in the penalty area to finish emphatically after being set up by Douvikas.

He then turned provider shortly after half time, releasing Lucas Da Cunha with a perfectly weighted pass for the visitors' fourth goal.

Ten minutes later, Paz supplied another assist for Douvikas, who completed his hat-trick as Lens's defence continued to unravel.

By the time the Argentine was withdrawn in the 58th minute, Como had scored six times, with their number 10 directly responsible for three of those goals.

His contribution followed an equally impressive performance against Manchester United on Matchday 3, when he scored twice and created another goal in a commanding 4-1 victory over Michael Carrick's side.

Those displays have propelled Paz to the top of the Champions League goal-involvement standings.

According to Opta, his eight direct contributions place him ahead of every other player in this season's competition, including Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane and Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal.

Paz also leads the tournament's assist chart with five, having supplied two against Manchester United and another two against Lens.

Only two players have registered more assists in their first four appearances of a single Champions League campaign: Real Madrid legend Raul in 2002-03 and former Barcelona forward Neymar in 2016-17, who both recorded six.

The figures illustrate how quickly Paz has established himself among Europe's most influential attacking midfielders.

His outstanding performances have not been limited to continental competition, either.

Across Serie A and the Champions League, the Argentine has contributed six goals and eight assists in 13 appearances this season, underlining his importance to Como's increasingly ambitious project.

Fabregas's team currently sit fourth in the Italian top flight and occupy the same position in the Champions League standings, having recovered emphatically from their defeat to Feyenoord.

For a club competing in Europe's elite competition for the first time, that progress has been exceptional.

However, Paz's individual development also raises an intriguing question about the plans of the European champions who originally brought him through their academy.

Real Madrid faced an important decision over Paz's future during the summer transfer window.

Having sold the midfielder to Como in 2024, Los Blancos retained contractual mechanisms allowing them to regain control of his future.

Reports initially suggested that the Spanish giants were preparing to activate an existing buy-back clause, potentially paving the way for a return to the Santiago Bernabeu.

However, the two clubs eventually reached a different agreement.

On June 29, Real Madrid officially announced that Paz would remain at Como for the 2026-27 season, a decision made at the player's own request.

Crucially, the agreement also confirmed that Madrid would retain a unilateral option to buy back his registration rights for the 2027-28 campaign.

That arrangement allowed Paz to continue playing regularly under Fabregas while preserving a route back to the Spanish capital.

The financial details were not disclosed in Madrid's official announcement, although Spanish newspaper AS reported that the agreement involved a €60m (£52m) transaction and an €80m (£69m) buy-back option for summer 2027.

Madrid's decision was understandable given the competition for attacking midfield positions in Jose Mourinho's squad.

Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler and Brahim Diaz are among the players capable of operating in similar areas, leaving no obvious guarantee that Paz would receive the minutes he currently enjoys at Como.

His Champions League performances nevertheless strengthen the argument that he is developing into a player capable of competing at the highest level.

Real Madrid have not announced any intention to bring him back ahead of schedule, and a recent report from AS indicated that the club would not make a decision on its buy-back options before next spring.

For now, Paz remains central to Fabregas's plans, with Como preparing to host AEK Athens in their next Champions League fixture on November 24.

Madrid's decision to allow him another season in Italy has already helped the Argentine reach new heights. His continued progress will only make the question of what happens in 2027 more compelling.

#1712. 'It's certainly possible': Erik ten Hag sticks the knife in on Man United and warns his old club they could get relegated after poor start to the season

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:26 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 06:41 EDT, 2 November 2026

Erik ten Hag has warned his former club Manchester United that they could get relegated this season as their dismal season shows no sign of improving currently.

The Red Devils languish outside the Premier League relegation zone only on goal difference, as they sit 17th with seven points from nine matches - two more than bottom side Sunderland.

United have staggeringly only won one match in the top-flight, a 5-2 win over Premier League new boys Ipswich Town, a Premier League low that is equalled with Sunderland and 19th-placed Nottingham Forest.

Their plight worsened on Saturday afternoon after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea - which saw them endure a second-half collapse and see Lisandro Martinez sent off.

As a result, pressure is mounting on under-fire head coach Michael Carrick and one of his predecessors Ten Hag – who won the Carabao Cup and the FA Cup during his two-and-a-bit seasons at United - believes the Old Trafford outfit could be mired in a relegation battle in the months to come.

'In the Premier League it's certainly possible, because all the teams are simply strong,' he said on ESPN NL, when asked about United's possibility of relegation.

Erik ten Hag has warned Manchester United that they could get relegated this season

Their 2-0 loss at Chelsea on Saturday means they're 17th - two points above 20th Sunderland

'They're all strong squads, all good managers. If you end up on the wrong side once and you really get into that vicious circle, then it can become very difficult.'

United have some tough fixtures coming up with a home encounter with Aston Villa on Sunday afternoon before a trip to bitter rivals Liverpool after the international break on November 22. After those two games, in-form Brentford travel to Old Trafford on November 28.

Ten Hag's comments come after his latest swipe at his former player Cristiano Ronaldo, claiming the Portugal icon's career was already over by the time he joined Juventus and eventually returned to Old Trafford.

'Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must also make way for the team. That was simply the problem with Ronaldo,' Ten Hag also told ESPN.

'Let there be no misunderstanding on my part, he is of course a great player. He belongs among the greats of the world.

'But the reality is also that he hasn't been able to deliver for the last seven or eight years. From Juventus onwards, it was simply over.'

#1711. Man United head coach Michael Carrick facing 'decisive' Premier League showdown with Aston Villa

By Matt Law | 05 Nov 2026 19:25, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 19:27

Manchester United are reportedly unlikely to appoint another interim head coach, should the club make the decision to relieve Michael Carrick of his duties at Old Trafford.

Carrick has kept his job with the 20-time English champions despite the fact that the team are currently sitting down in 17th spot in the Premier League table.

Man United recorded a morale-boosting 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday but have not triumphed in the league since the end of August.

Carrick's future is far from secure, with the club said to be weighing up all options available to them ahead of the November international break.

There have been suggestions that Man United could bring in an interim head coach to replace Carrick, with a long-term appointment then being made this summer.

However, according to Sky Sports News, that is unlikely to be a route that the club will take.

Sunday's Premier League clash with Aston Villa is seen as vital for Carrick's future - another win would almost certainly see the Englishman remain in charge.

However, a defeat could lead to the club deciding to sack the 45-year-old.

Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Antonio Conte are all still available for an immediate start, while there have also been claims that Didier Deschamps has been contacted.

Deschamps is available following his exit from France after the 2026 World Cup.

However, a manager high up their shortlist, Unai Emery, is now close to signing a new long-term contract with Aston Villa.

Cesc Fabregas is also said to have admirers at Man United due to his excellent work at Como, but a move to Old Trafford in the middle of the campaign is unlikely.

Man United have a record of one win, four draws and four defeats from their nine matches in the Premier League this season, with their only domestic victory of the campaign coming at the end of August at home to Ipswich Town.

#1710. GdS: Milan to sign record-breaking €500m deal with Adidas – the details

There has been talk about AC Milan moving to Adidas in recent weeks and that has now gone a step further, with details of the deal filtering.

By all accounts, next year will see Milan end their partnership with Puma. The two have worked together since 2018 – when the Rossoneri stopped working with the iconic German brand – and produced several kits in that time.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, with a focus on improving commercial value, Gerry Cardinale has now looked to the kit and decided to head back to what some may call home.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the Diavolo will sign a blockbuster deal with the three-stripe brand, worth €500 million across 10 seasons. In other words, they’ll earn a record-breaking €50m per season, as opposed to the reported €30m.

A deal with potential for ‘exponential growth’, it’s a €36m increase on the current contract with Puma – worth €14m per season – and significantly changes the value of the shirt. Looking elsewhere, Juventus’ deal with Adidas is believed to be worth €408m across 10 seasons, whilst Inter’s eight-year deal was worth €30m per season.

Above all, though, it’s a romantic return and a symbol of hope to return to better times. Throughout the history of their partnership, Milan have often been at the top, and it’s one of the most recognisable relationships in Italian (and European) football. Now, it’s coming back.

#1709. RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: Here's what I've heard privately about Max Dowman that proves he will come out of Mikel Arteta scolding a stronger player - and why he'll have dealt with far worse already

Published: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 06:47 EDT, 2 November 2026

Mikel Arteta didn’t require the hysteria of the past week to know a thing or two about dubious reactions. Before we get onto his reaction to Max Dowman’s reaction, or the wider reaction to those reactions, we might revisit something that happened in November 2010.

That’s a long journey into the past, but the episode tells us a little about Arteta’s feelings for opponents who took liberties with his shins. The abbreviated version: violence would be returned with spectacular amounts of interest.

The longer telling revolves around a match between Arteta’s Everton and West Brom. To rewatch some of the footage now, we would say Gonzalo Jara brought it upon himself after 58 minutes, when in a mad passage he elbowed Leighton Baines and then barged shoulder-first into Steven Pienaar in the same scramble for a loose ball.

The defining act came next – Arteta stepped in to retrieve possession, but was clattered by Jara with one of those nasty scissor-motion tackles that could break the standing leg. If that sounds familiar, it’s because the challenge was near-identical to the lunge by Fleetwood Town’s Harrison Neal that provoked Dowman on Tuesday night.

But Arteta didn’t kick Jara, as Dowman did Neal. No, he stomped on his leg. Twice, actually. And with venom in each.

Arsenal's 16-year-old Max Dowman gets an earful from his manager Mikel Arteta after the attacker was sent off on Tuesday night against Fleetwood

It was a frustrating night for Dowman who failed to live up to the excitement that surrounds him

Dowman was around 11 months old when this happened, so he’ll have no idea about all that. And besides, he’d probably be wise to avoid bringing it up. Aged 16, his sense of which battles to pick will be growing by the hour.

But Arteta was 28 when he turned vigilante against West Brom. And it wasn’t quite an isolated incident.

Seven months earlier, Morten Gamst Pedersen stepped on Arteta’s ankle in a game against Blackburn and the Spaniard didn’t like it. His response? He poked Pedersen in the eye and got a yellow.

So let’s offer a couple of conclusions at this point.

One is about Arteta – if he wishes to present himself as a poster boy for the zen state and self-control in football matches, then he might need to torch a few archives. The two yellow cards he has collected on the touchline this season would suggest his own journey to enlightenment is ongoing.

The second, more meaningful conclusion centres on the general theme that Dowman should have been preserved from a few chilly words and a colder stare from his manager.

In the aftermath of Arsenal’s defeat at Fleetwood, that peculiar stance has been propagated by Paul Merson and Gabby Agbonlahor, who were among the vocal cohort that bristled and recoiled at the sight of a young pro being sent to the dressing room without a cuddle. The backlash against Arteta almost sounded as if he had abdicated a duty of care. Of all the reactions in this saga, I found that the strangest.

When Arteta addressed the matter on Friday, his justification felt far closer to the mark: ‘You have to understand the context. We’re not in Disneyland, we’re in the Premier League.'

If Arteta wishes to present himself as a poster boy for the zen state and self-control in football matches, then he might wish to explain why he gets booked so often

Morten Gamst Pedersen is left reeling after a clash with Arteta in his Everton days. A few years later Arteta would poke Pedersen in the eye during a game at Ewood Park

A hypocrite on the subject of retaliations? Yes, we can go with that. Wrong in his handling of a young player who lost his cool? No. Definitely not.

At 16, we can say Dowman meets the legal definition of a child, and a bloody talented one at that, but he’s not a kid. Kids don’t get into the Arsenal first team. Kids wouldn’t survive the hothouse of a Premier League academy.

To understand why that might be, it is instructive to look back to an update on the Arsenal website from the summer. On June 4, as they do every year, they put out a few words to detail which of their Under 18s and Under 21s had not made the grade, which was a list that included the names of Harrison Dudziak, Seb Ferdinand, Cam’ron Ismail, Will Sweet and Josh Nichols.

As very good players, they were all in the Arsenal Under 19s squad in 2024, when Dowman, aged 14, became the youngest scorer in the UEFA Youth League's history against Atalanta.

Of the starting XI that day, only four remain at Arsenal, and the point is this – Dowman has lived through the brutalities of that whittling process every summer and he will have been friends with those who had their dreams ended.

He will have been hardened by their traumas and solidified by knowing what it takes to stay standing in that world.

In short, when we attempt to imagine his position, and wonder how a cold shoulder might feel to a Gen Z child in the Arsenal team, we do so without the relevant context.

Because Dowman was never in Disneyland. A Premier League academy, even an excellent and caring one like that at Arsenal, will inevitably be more like a trip to the Hunger Games. Dowman has been there since he was five, so let’s assume it will take more than a mildly disappointed manager to hurt his feelings.

An incensed Dowman grapples with the Fleetwood Town players just before being sent off on Tuesday night

Dowman has not appeared flustered while he has passed milestones at breakneck speed in his short career so far

Based on everything I’ve heard privately and publicly about Dowman, his reaction to the reaction chain will go the other way. He’s a tremendously promising player and has a strong mind with good people behind him – it’s why he has not been flustered by any of the milestones he has passed at breakneck speed.

The wobbles, like the one at Fleetwood and shortly before that with England Under 19s, are few. But they are also useful, based on the truism that we all learn more when things go wrong. Viewed through that lens, Arteta’s worst possible response would be to indulge a blip or pretend it never happened. As an excellent manager, he hasn’t done that.

It is too early to say how far Dowman will go in his career. Likewise, we have no idea if he will shape into the kind of player who jabs a finger into the occasional eye or plants studs in any thighs. His reaction to Neal on Tuesday was certainly at the Disney-end of that scale.

But Dowman’s chances of succeeding will only be increased by learning where the margins exist. As with a few other facets of his game, he is ahead of the curve.

A confession: I find the Kylian Mbappe ‘dictator’ memes funny. If you haven’t seen them, the gist is pretty simple – someone once decided that he carries himself like a dictator and subsequently imposed his head on the bodies and uniforms of a few notorious figures from history.

One of those was Chairman Mao Zedong and Mbappe’s own amusement at that fact is why he was forced onto the journey of 1,000 apologies this week.

In China, where it remains taboo to query Mao’s actions in any way, Mbappe has since had multiple sponsorships cancelled and a diplomatic row has swirled, with the upshot that a state-controlled broadcaster is now refusing to screen his matches.

The space here is too short to relitigate the deaths of millions of people under Mao’s reign, but Mbappe might have cause to wonder if he ever really needed Chinese money that badly.

Kylian Mbappe got himself into hot water this week by finding a Chairman Mao meme amusing. He has now had sponsorship deals in China canned

Aside from saying he is ‘proud’ to be going back, Garcia adds that he is ‘excited’ to ‘strengthen personal relationships’ with those he left behind in 2022.

Based on multiple conversations I have had with leading players from the Tour, including a well-known name who has regularly described Garcia as a ‘total a**e’ since his defection, that excitement is remarkably one-sided.

#1708. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1707. JJ Gabriel future: Real Madrid 'map out' pathway for Man United wonderkid into first team at Bernabeu

By Matt Law | 05 Nov 2026 19:41, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 19:44

Real Madrid have reportedly already mapped out a pathway for JJ Gabriel into the first team at Bernabeu, as Los Blancos close in on a deal for the Manchester United wonderkid.

Man United have finally admitted defeat when it comes to the 16-year-old, who informed the club in September of his desire to seek pastures new.

Barcelona, Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs to be linked with JJ Gabriel, but it is understood that Real Madrid are now close to an agreement, with the teenager expected to move to Bernabeu at the start of 2027.

According to The Telegraph, Real Madrid want to initially use JJ Gabriel in their Castilla outfit, who operate in Spain's third division.

However, the report claims that the teenager will not have to wait long to secure first-team action in either La Liga or the Champions League.

JJ Gabriel made his senior debut for Man United in their pre-season game against Atletico Madrid during the summer, but he is yet to feature for the first team in a competitive match.

The attacker had been due to sign scholarship terms with the Red Devils on his 16th birthday last month, with a professional contract then expected to follow a year later.

However, JJ Gabriel's representatives informed Man United in September that the youngster would be looking to leave the club as soon as possible.

JJ Gabriel has a deal with Man United's academy until the end of the campaign, but the teenager has a European passport through both of his parents, and a FIFA loophole could see him join Real Madrid at the start of 2027.

JJ Gabriel is one of the most talented youngsters in world football, and there is no question that his imminent exit is a major blow for Man United.

The attacker boasts a record of 29 goals and four assists in 32 appearances for Man United Under-18s, while he has scored twice and registered two assists in two appearances for Man United Under-21s in the Premier League 2.

Initially, Man United had been hopeful of convincing JJ Gabriel and his representatives to reverse the decision.

However, JJ Gabriel has not been at Carrington since September, showing his clear desire to move on, with the attacker training in Spain ahead of an expected move to Madrid.

#1706. A chance for rotation and rest as we face Fleetwood Town

We’re in EFL Cup action this evening, taking on Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium (not that one). Tonight’s opposition sit 18th in League Two, and this will surely influence Mikel Arteta’s team selection. There are players I just do not want to see this evening. Not just from the start, but not in the squad at all.

The likes of Declan Rice, Gabriel, Ezri Konsa, Martin Odegaard have all played a lot and could use a night off, and I would also include the two wide players we have fit – Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze. With injuries to Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis, we’re very light in that area of the pitch, and we do not need to risk them in a game like this. There’s still plenty of scope for rotation, and there are some senior players who could use some minutes, as well as an opportunity to fill out the bench with Academy lads.

You imagine we’ll see starts for Kepa, Martin Zubimendi (assuming his nose isn’t too sore after the weekend), Cristhian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie, Mikel Merino, maybe Jurrien Timber, Myles Lewis-Skelly, and possibly Bruno Guimaraes, but also it’s an opportunity for Marli Salmon and Max Dowman again, both of whom started in the last round against Ipswich. Dowman played centrally that evening, in the Odegaard role, and got two goals, but I wonder if tonight he might be used out wide as we rest Madueke.

After that, young players like Ife Ibrahim and Theo Julienne will be hoping for minutes to add to the ones they picked up in the last round, while forwards like Ceadach O’Neill and Igor Tyjon might fancy their chances of being included. This is a kind draw ahead of a weekend trip to Anfield, and with Liverpool playing Chelsea tomorrow night, it’s an opportunity for the manager to ease the burden on the guys who have played a lot as well as giving the next generation a chance too.

I think we’ll also see Viktor Gyokeres up front, and the Swedish international could really do with a goal. He’s on a barren streak (in club terms at least), that stretches back to May 2nd, and it’s now 15 games without a goal. Even though his minutes have been a bit scant this season, that’s a record that’s hanging over him and one he’ll want to put right. A goal, or goals, against a League Two side in this competition will always have that little caveat applied, but it ought to be a real opportunity for him to build a little goalscoring confidence, so fingers crossed he can do exactly that.

Speaking about tonight’s game, Arteta said:

Every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve to do that, and then try to win and try to play better than them.

So, let’s see how it plays out later on, kick off is 20.00 in this part of the world.

Elsewhere, while I find the concept of individual awards in football completely counter-intuitive to what makes the game as compelling as it is, I did want to mention Bukayo Saka winning the Socrates Award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony last night. The official website reports that: “Bukayo and his family have worked with multiple charities, including long-term projects with Big Shoe, providing medical care and humanitarian aid for children and families in need in London and around the world.”

And yet, they are often held up as an example of people who earn too much for doing too little. I remember during Covid, politicians singled out football players as those who should set an example by taking wage cuts or making charity donations or supporting the health services, while ignoring those who – less publicly – earn far, far more. But as we can see here, someone like Bukayo Saka (and he’s far from alone too), uses what his talent has provided to help others, and while I’m sure he doesn’t do it for awards or recognition, this spotlight on what he does can help the causes he supports.

This is an individual award worth highlighting, and you can see the ceremony and his speech about it below.

Right, I’m gonna leave it there for now. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool new matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

#1703. Tottenham told to hijack Man City move for £12.5m Pedro Porro replacement

By Ben Knapton | 05 Nov 2026 19:46

Tottenham Hotspur have been urged to hijack Manchester City's proposed move for the "fantastic" Alexander Freeman amid speculation over the Villarreal defender's future.

The 22-year-old has only seen his stock rise since moving to La Liga from Orlando in January, and he was the USA's starting right-back throughout the 2026 World Cup.

Man City and Tottenham have been the most heavily linked with a transfer in recent weeks, and the former received an apparent boost earlier this month, when it was reported that Freeman is open to moving to the Etihad in 2027.

However, Tottenham have also expressed an interest in the 2004-born full-back, currently managed by ex-Spurs head coach Mauricio Pochettino for the national team.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, ex-Tottenham and USA goalkeeper Brad Friedel revealed his personal connection with Freeman and talked up the prospect of the defender joining Roberto De Zerbi's side.

"Alex is a really good player and a really good kid," Friedel said. "I know Alex's family and I think he has the quality to be in the Premier League, that's for sure.

"Whether it's a team that, because De Zerbi is going to want to be in the Champions League, whether it's there, it's yet to be seen.

"But I think that could be a really interesting recruitment strategy, but one that they need to take their time on and really look. But character-wise, Alex is fantastic and it would be brilliant to see him line up at Spurs."

Freeman - who can also play as a left-back, centre-back and right-winger - has made 15 appearances for Villarreal across all competitions this season, setting up one goal.

The 22-year-old also scored one goal and set up one more for the USA at the World Cup, netting in their 2-0 group-stage win over Australia, while previously bagging a brace in a 5-1 friendly victory over Hoffenheim.

Freeman - who is valued at €15m (£12.5m) by Transfermarkt - would currently face major competition for Tottenham minutes behind Pedro Porro, Archie Gray, Destiny Udogie and Andy Robertson, while Souza will return from his Porto loan spell in 2027.

However, Porro's future remains clouded in uncertainty, as the Spain World Cup winner has been linked with switches to both Barcelona and Real Madrid in recent times.

Porro has opened the door to a return to La Liga one day, although Tottenham are under no immediate pressure to sell the defender, who signed a new contract to 2031 back in June.

Should the Lilywhites fail to secure European football for 2027-28, though, Porro could be tempted by a big-money switch to Camp Nou or the Bernabeu, vacating a spot for Freeman to fill his boots.

Brad Friedel was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of Grosvenor Sport.

#1701. Former Premier League manager Pepe Mel, 63, recovering in intensive care after suffering stroke as former clubs offer support

Published: 07:42 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 07:45 EDT, 2 November 2026

Former West Brom boss Pepe Mel is recovering in intensive care after undergoing surgery following a stroke.

Mel's former club Real Betis, who he managed in two different spells, announced at the request of his family that Mel suffered a stroke on Sunday and subsequently underwent surgery.

The operation was successful with Mel, 63, now recovering in intensive care at the Virgen del Rocio Hospital in Seville.

Mel has largely coached in Spain during his managerial career, but had a short spell in charge of West Brom.

The Spanish coach took over the club in January 2014 when they were four points above the Premier League relegation zone, with the Baggies having sacked Steve Clarke the previous month.

Mel took charge of 17 matches during his time at the Hawthorns, winning three, drawing six and losing eight.

West Brom ultimately finished 17th in the Premier League, with the Baggies ending three points above relegated Norwich.

Mel was sacked 24 hours after the final day of the season.

Former West Brom boss Pepe Mel is recovering in intensive care following a stroke

His brief spell in charge included having to deal with the aftermath of several dramatic incidents.

West Brom had sacked striker Nicolas Anelka after the veteran forward announced he was quitting the club, having been fined and suspended over his controversial ‘quenelle’ goal celebration.

Mel also needed to handle the fallout following a dressing room bust-up between Saido Berahino and James Morrison.

The Spaniard ultimately returned to Real Betis for a second spell later in 2014 and led the club to promotion back to LaLiga for the second time, having done so for the first time in 2011.

He had also previously led Rayo Vallecano to promotion to Spain's second tier.

Mel's former clubs have been among those to offer him support following his surgery.

'From Rayo Vallecano, we want to convey all our support and affection to Pepe Mel, after suffering a stroke for which he has had to undergo surgery. We wish him a swift and complete recovery,' a Rayo Vallecano statement read.

'From LALIGA we send all our affection and a speedy recovery to Pepe Mel. We're with you, Pepe,' LaLiga shared.

Mel, who has coached 16 different clubs during his managerial career, was last in charge of Moroccan side IR Tanger but left earlier this year.
