#1646. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

#1645. Report: Arsenal star's agents seek bombshell transfer to Liverpool

We could well see one Arsenal star move to Liverpool. His agents have sought a move and made contact with the Reds.

Arsenal and Liverpool have found themselves as rivals over the last few years, even if they haven’t actually battled in a serious title race yet. The Gunners ultimately didn’t come close to stopping the Reds in 2025, while Liverpool’s efforts in 2026 were even worse.

Yet, there’s a sense that this is the title fight for the next few years. If Liverpool can sort themselves out anyway, and we wait on the outcome of Manchester City’s guilty verdict.

As a result, no one should really expect much transfer activity between the two. Even if you don’t rate one of your players, sending them to a rival who does rate them is a recipe for disaster. It usually just means you’re undervaluing your player, in fact.

But that’s not to say it’s impossible. One Arsenal star, it’s reported, has been in contact with Liverpool over a possible move.

Martin Zubimendi to Liverpool?Liverpool tried to sign Martin Zubimendi in 2024 from Real Sociedad. It was Arne Slot's first summer and the Reds felt he was the ideal player for the new head coach. Zubimendi, however, pulled out of the deal at the last minute and remained with La Real for another year. He'd then move to Arsenal in 2025, having decided to make a big move after all. That ended successfully for Zubimendi to an extent. He was a key part of their Premier League title success but Arsenal have already replaced him. The Spaniard now barely plays and the Gunners are willing to sell.

Liverpool tried to sign Martin Zubimendi in 2024 from Real Sociedad. It was Arne Slot's first summer and the Reds felt he was the ideal player for the new head coach.

Zubimendi, however, pulled out of the deal at the last minute and remained with La Real for another year. He'd then move to Arsenal in 2025, having decided to make a big move after all.

That ended successfully for Zubimendi to an extent. He was a key part of their Premier League title success but Arsenal have already replaced him. The Spaniard now barely plays and the Gunners are willing to sell.

We've already called that a mistake on their part and one that Liverpool should take advantage of. It appears the opportunity is there, too.

TeamTalk claim that Zubimendi's representatives have contacted Liverpool about a possible move. It's not really known if the Reds are willing to make an offer at this stage, nor can we say what the price tag would be, but there is a chance of it happening.

Zubimendi almost certainly moves in 2027. Liverpool almost certainly sign a midfielder, too. Whether that's a 27-year-old, though, is another matter - such a signing would go against everything they've been doing lately.

Still, we believe he's the ideal fit for this team and exactly what's needed in the middle. Honestly, if Zubimendi and Arsenal are willing, Liverpool would be silly not to bid.

#1644. Barnsley vs Aldershot Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 05 Nov 2026 22:18

Aldershot Town will set out to pull off an FA Cup first-round upset in South Yorkshire on Saturday, when they visit Oakwell to take on third-tier Barnsley.

The hosts enter at this stage while their visitors took part in the final qualifying round and needed a replay to progress.

Barnsley head into FA Cup action for the first time this season on Saturday in need of a victory to arrest a slump in the early stages of 2026-27.

The Reds reached the third round of this competition last year, falling in a trip to Liverpool, but begin their new campaign with just four wins from 17 competitive matches so far this term with all of those coming in the first six outings.

They did enjoy a positive start to life back under returning boss Daniel Stendel but are now winless in 11 games since early September, losing nine of those including four straight league defeats heading into the weekend.

Stendel's men were, at least, able to end that rut at home to Oxford United on Saturday, drawing 1-1 thanks to Vimal Yoganathan's opener having been down to 10 men inside 10 minutes, but the South Yorkshire side still sit 23rd in League One with just nine points on the board from 12 games having conceded 22 goals.

With positives to take from the weekend's display but real cause for concern around their recent months, Barnsley will be desperate to avoid an upset at the weekend and taste victory at Oakwell.

Their opponents, meanwhile, make the trip north having scraped through the final qualifying round in the FA Cup.

Aldershot Town entered this year's competition in the fourth and final round of qualifying, taking on ninth-tier Tadley Calleva, but they were only able to draw 2-2 at home before prevailing in a 2-0 triumph on the road in the replay.

That eventual cup win broke up a five-game losing run in the National League for the Shots, who also headed into the weekend in the midst of a rut, but they bounced back to winning ways at home to Gateshead, as Brody Peart scored the only goal inside five minutes.

Scott Davies's side climbed back up to 14th spot in the fifth tier with that result, and now on the back of a midweek National League Cup loss to Ipswich Town Under-21s, they will hope to defy the odds at Oakwell on Saturday to reach the FA Cup second round for just the second time since 2015.

Barnsley are set to remain without attackers Ben Hamed Toure and Fabio Jalo on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Stendel should field a near full-strength XI with the Reds desperate for a win to turn their fortunes round, meaning star man Reyes Cleary should continue on the wing, while Tobi Adeyemo was injured early on Saturday and may be replaced up front by Rylan Brownlie.

Veteran and recent signing Daniel Johnson may be afforded a start in midfield alongside either Luca Connell or Patrick Kelly, while Jack Shepherd is available at the back despite being sent off last time out in the league.

Aldershot Town will field a similar starting XI from last week's league win over Gateshead.

Marcus Dinanga and Marcus Wyllie will both hope to start in attack, but if they continue with a 4-2-3-1 shape the line should again be led by Tristan Abrahams, who has scored six goals so far this season.

A summer of plenty of change added several key men to their ranks, with Michael Stickland and Kiki Oshilaja now mainstays in defence and Dominic Odusanya and Conor Lawless likely to continue a midfield partnership if the latter is fit having been forced off last weekend.

Slicker; Kay, Gale, Shepherd, Larkeche; Connell, Johnson; Yoganathan, McGeegan, Cleary; Brownlie

Hayes; Stickland, Oshilaja, Dyce, Harfield; Lawless, Odusanya; Peart, Tuma, Sandah; Abrahams

Barnsley could certainly be vulnerable to a cup upset at home, given their poor league record and struggles at both ends of the pitch and growing concern around the club, but needing a win to start turning their form around, we do expect Stendel's men to outclass their non-league visitors.

#1643. On The Road: From Hagi and Popescu to Danny Armstrong... football in Bucharest has history and hope

Published: 16:31 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 12:42 EDT, 2 November 2026

The Starbucks at the entrance to the Old Town makes a familiar point by its very presence. The Half-Time Bar roars a modern truth incessantly.

Bucharest 2026, beneath the enduring glitz of imperial time and amid the clinging grip of post-communism, has become marked by globalism.

Starbucks serves its universal wares and the Half-Time Bar resounds to the English Premier League. Yet the fabulous gems of Romanian football are not far away.

The Muzeul Fotbalului sits on the edge of the Old Town. It is starkly modern. Its four floors offer strips to buy, interactive displays to goggle at and fiddle with, and shirts to admire or even covet. There are strips worn by Maradona, Pele, Cruyff and Ronaldo. But there is Romanian history too.

Gheorghe Hagi, Gheorghe Popescu and Cristian Chivu are rightly celebrated. The wonderful run by the national team to the quarter-finals of the World Cup is recalled in full, glorious colour.

There is a tribute to Helmuth Duckadam, who is the only goalkeeper to have saved four penalties in a Champions League final. When Steaua Bucharest defeated Barcelona in a penalty shoot-out in 1986, since you ask. Incidentally, Miodrag Belodedici is the only Romanian to win the Champions League twice, once with Steaua and then with Red Star in 1991.

Scottish winger Danny Armstrong scored in Dinamo Bucharest's 2-0 win over UTA Arad

'That era is gone. It is not coming back any time soon,' says Jo, dishing out tickets while fielding questions from visitors.

Football was strong under communist rule with star players tied to clubs and only allowed to leave for abroad at the behest of the government. Steaua was the team of the ministry of defence, Dinamo Bucharest was the team of the police. Both ruled the roost. Two years before Steaua won the Champions League, Dinamo lost in the semi-finals.

Now Steaua has been rent asunder. It is now called FCSB after a legal dispute over ownership of its name after a takeover by Gigi Becali. Dinamo have not won the title since 2006. Both seem to be haunted by old glories.

'I am Steaua,' says Jo. 'I always will be. My father was too. He said to me I had a choice: 'Support Steaua or sleep outside'.'

But Jo accepts that the best that can be hoped for is a minor renaissance in the national side.

'Club football at the highest level is simply about money and there is little of that here,' he says.

The verdict is more gloomy from Toni. With desultory glances towards Manchester City against Brighton playing out on multiple screens in the Half-Time Bar, the student says: 'The only team we have in European football this season is Universitatea (of Craiova). The others went out in qualifying. Steaua, for example, could not even qualify for the European Conference League. Universitatea is in that. That's where we are.'

There is no sneering from this Scot. 'Look at your country,' he says. 'Maybe a little bit better but nowhere near what it was.'

Dinamo Bucharest have not won the league for 20 years, but they have a passionate support

Ion, an older gentleman, interjects. 'It is a cabal now,' he says of European competition. 'Maybe good for the TV but only four or five teams outside of England can win it.'

But he adds: 'I am Dinamo. I still go. You will see what it means tomorrow.'

The Sunday game against UTA Arad is certainly compelling. There is a large crowd with an excellent atmosphere. But the cup tie last Wednesday against Chindia Targoviste was instructive for this observer.

It showcased what was still impressive about the Romanian game. It was possible, too, to have conversation with supporters as the cup is not taken too seriously at this stage and the crowd was only a few thousand.

The venue was the National Arena as the Dinamo Stadium is being rebuilt. The National Stadium is a wonderful arena, far better than anything we have to offer in Scotland. On Wednesday, as the rains thundered in Bucharest, the closed roof offered what seemed like a view of the stars but was, in fact, an array of lights peppering the modern protection from elements.

My accent invited conversation. 'Ah, a Scotsman,' muttered a companion in the splendid stand. 'Thank you for coming. It is good that Romanian football can be spoken about elsewhere.'

There was particular pleasure at my identity. 'Danny Armstrong is simply our hero,' says Nick, an engineer, who is at the game with his son and his friend Piti. 'He is the best player in the country and we will enjoy him while we can. Why does he not play for the national team?'

The answer to this is debated but there is no room for argument with Armstrong's impact on the Superliga since his move from Kilmarnock. 'It is not only goals and assists,' says Nick. 'He leads the team so well by his example. He is not in the team tonight because he is too important to risk in this fixture. If we are in trouble, he might come on but I don't foresee this.'

Gheorghe Hagi is among the Romanian legends celebrated at Bucharest's Muzeul Fotbalului

He is right. Dinamo win 5-2 and Armstrong remains on the bench. The player is thus fresh to give Mailsport an exclusive interview the next day. This is coming soon to a sports page near you but no spoiler alert is needed to reveal that the Scot is relishing his opportunity in the Romanian capital.

He is the fans' darling. And Dinamo, despite their recent lack of success, have a strong, impassioned support. 'This club has struggled and we have not won the league for 20 years,' says Piti. 'But there was even once a threat to our existence a few years ago but the fans pulled together.'

He points out that supporters would buy three tickets each for a game just to help Dinamo pay the bills. 'We put everything we could in. I know football is really just bread and circuses so success is not too important to me. But the existence of the club is. That's important.'

Dinamo stood for the opposition to the Ceausescu regime under communism. 'Steaua was run by Nicu, the son of Nicolae, the leader of the country. So it was regarded as the team of the regime and obviously it had strong links to the military. Dinamo was the team many dissenters backed.'

That was then. This is now. The team has strong designs on the title. 'With Danny we can do anything,' says Nick.

This sentiment was reinforced tonight. Armstrong walked on the pitch carrying his two-year-old daughter, Darby. He left to an ovation with minutes remaining, having scored a beautiful opener in their 2-0 victory. These are good days for the player and the fans who love him.

#1641. Report: Julian Ward willing to let Liverpool star go

Julian Ward has a lot of decisions to make about Liverpool ahead of his first transfer window as their sporting director.

The Englishman took over the role from Richard Hughes after he chose to join Al-Hilal upon the completion of the 2026-27 summer transfer window.

Liverpool have already spent well over £150 million this season so, any other additions will need to be worthwhile.

Many different players have been linked with an Anfield switch but, with how poor Liverpool have been this term, they must make sure that every signing they agree is one that makes sense.

Even if that means some of their own players are going to have be put on the chopping block.

Liverpool are happy to let Federico Chiesa exit Anfield in January

Federico Chiesa is one of the most likely players to leave Liverpool this January.

The attacker has only been given a few minutes of playing time by Andoni Iraola and, since Arne Slot failed to give him all that much either, it's clear that the end of his time in L4 is upon us.

Of course, there have been some moments when he's stood out from the crowd but, he's failed to make enough of an impact to keep his place.

His exit has been discussed for some time now with Inter Milan being linked with the Italian's transfer once again.

"Inter are considering a move for Liverpool winger Federico Chiesa as they look to add a fifth forward to their squad in the January transfer window," Tribuna wrote.

"According to Tribuna.com sources, the Italian winger is emerging as one of the options being considered by the Nerazzurri. Chiesa has struggled for regular playing time at Liverpool and could be open to returning to Serie A.

"Liverpool would be willing to discuss a loan deal with an option to buy, with the permanent transfer fee set at around €8-10 million."

Liverpool must make sure they have enough depth in attack to sell Federico Chiesa

At the moment, most of Liverpool's injuries have happened to their attackers.

Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak have both spent extended time on the sidelines this term and, while others such as Lewis Koumas and Rio Ngumoha are preferred over him, it's still nice for Liverpool to know that they have someone who's scored 83 goals across his career on their bench.

However, much like Slot, Iraola has chosen against giving Chiesa a decent amount of playing time so, it's clear that he's not in his immediate plans.

But, despite this, if a massive injury crisis occurs, the Reds need to be sure that they have enough firepower to continue shooting themselves up the table.

If not, they could go into free fall and end up even worse off than they were last term which is something that they certainly won't want to happen.

#1640. Report: Liverpool ready to make £83m offer for midfielder who is 'not normal'

Andoni Iraola still has a lot of work to do on his Liverpool squad.

At the moment, the Reds are fifth in the Premier League table and are currently nine points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

After the performances of both teams last season, it's clear to see why the gap between both clubs is so large.

However, with the appointment of Iraola and the extra £150 million that was spent on new players by Liverpool this summer, fans thought that things could end up being different this season.

But, now that we're just a few months in, it's clear that more change is needed and that the Anfield outfit need to dip their toes into the January transfer market when that chance arises.

Liverpool prepare £83 million offer for Federico Valverde

Liverpool's midfield is probably their main area that needs upgrading.

At the moment, Trey Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister are their two best-performing central midfielders and, since Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch can't play alongside one another in the double pivot, some serious questions are being asked.

The fact that Szoboszlai and Gravenberch have just been handed new long-term deals also throws a major spanner into the works.

However, after the first few months of the 2026-27 season, it's clear that Liverpool's recruitment team also see their midfielder as a major problem with Spanish outlet Fichajes now sharing that the Reds are "preparing" an £83 million offer for Real Madrid's Federico Valverde.

"Liverpool are interested in signing Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde and are preparing a €100 million offer to secure his transfer in the upcoming summer transfer window," they wrote.

"Liverpool's primary target is a midfielder who can fill the void left by Alexis Mac Allister."

Federico Valverde would be a game-changing signing for Liverpool

Although Valverde's best position is as a central midfielder, Jose Mourinho has been using him as more of a right-back this season.

Real Madrid may have signed Trent Alexander-Arnold and Denzel Dumfries to cover right-back over the last couple of transfer windows but, after their recent performances, it's clear that the Special One isn't happy.

So, that's why Valverde has been used there instead.

This sort of versatility is key and is one of the main things that Liverpool seem to be looking for in their new recruits.

And, since his teammates have constantly lauded him throughout his career with Guille Varela even calling his performances "not normal," it's clear that he'd be a top signing for any club.

Indeed, £83 million is a lot for one player but, when Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak cost Liverpool a combined total of £248 million, it's clear that transfer fees are going to continue to sky rocket.

Here's hoping Liverpool don't splash all their cash at once.

#1639. The town of Clydebank knows all about triumphs and traumas. Now a little Blitz spirit is helping their defiant football team rise to prominence once again

Published: 12:23 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EDT, 2 November 2026

Five framed photographs hang on the walls of the clubhouse lounge at Holm Park: the Titan crane, the Singer sewing factory and Kilbowie Park, as well as the rubble-strewn streets of the Blitz and the long-lost Seven Seas pub. Together, they tell the story of a town, its triumphs and its traumas.

‘There’s an old Bankies song,’ says Clydebank FC chair Grace McGibbon, who had the pictures installed at the start of this season. ‘It goes, “We make ships, sewing machines, we build famous football teams, we’re the Bankies from Kilbowie Park”. It’s kind of a homage to that.’

To McGibbon, the pictures are a reminder of what Clydebank is and has always been.

‘Clydebank is not just a football team, or a shopping centre, or whatever else you might think,’ she tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s so much more than any of that. This is a community that never gives up. There’s almost a defiance about the place. That’s what these photos represent.

‘Other people might look at it and go, “It’s just pictures on a wall, I don’t get it”. But we get it. It reminds us why we’re here and why we’re doing this.’

Without question, ‘this’ is one of the Scottish football stories of the season so far. As well as being in contention for the Lowland League West title – and with it, the chance of a Lazarus-like return to the Scottish football league – Clydebank have reached the third round of the Scottish Cup for the third successive season where Championship side Livingston await.

Clydebank finished top of a KDM Evolution Trophy league phase containing mainly senior sides

More immediately, they host League One strugglers Alloa Athletic in the last 32 of the KDM Evolution Trophy on Tuesday, the Bankies having qualified for the knockout stages of the Challenge Cup by finishing top of the league phase, unbeaten, and ahead of the likes of Ross County, Airdrieonians and Cove Rangers.

Be under no illusions: something special is happening in West Dunbartonshire just now. To fully understand how special requires a short history lesson. Between 1888 and 1931, three clubs bearing the Clydebank name came and went. It was in the 1960s that things changed materially.

Frustrated by poor attendances, and inspired by Major League Baseball franchise relocations, Jack and Charlie Steedman – the majority owners of East Stirlingshire FC – merged their club with Clydebank Juniors. ES Clydebank, as they were called, relocated to New Kilbowie Park in Clydebank, enraging supporters of the hitherto Falkirk-based East Stirlingshire.

A legal challenge brought by local shareholders saw the merger invalidated and the brothers being deposed. Undeterred, they formed a brand-new club, Clydebank FC, which successfully applied for entry into the Scottish football league in time for the 1966/67 season. A decade later, inspired by a 20-year-old Davie Cooper, the club was promoted to the Premier Division for the first time, narrowly missing out on the First Division title to Alex Ferguson’s St Mirren.

For a while, everything was gravy. The Bankies established themselves as a solid if unspectacular outfit, represented at various times by the likes of Owen Coyle, Tommy Coyne and Bobby Williamson. The ‘two Jims’, Fallon and Gallacher, became club icons alongside record-goalscorer Ken Eadie. Gary Teale rose through the club’s youth academy. They even lured Cooper home to see out his career.

Kilbowie Park was one of the iconic stops for away fans before it was razed to the ground

In 1996, the rug was pulled. The Steedmans sold New Kilbowie Park to developers who demolished the ground and built a retail park on top of it. That sparked a chain of events that included ground-sharing with Dumbarton and Greenock Morton, ownership changes, and ill-conceived plans to relocate to Dublin, then Carlisle, the Scottish Borders and more.

After the inevitable tumble into administration, the club was acquired by the newly formed Airdrie United, itself a product of the liquidated Airdrieonians. To all intents and purposes, Clydebank FC was renamed and relocated, leaving devastated Bankies without a club.

McGibbon remembers it well. ‘I’m Clydebank born and bred,’ she beams. ‘My husband had been a Clydebank fan all his days and, when we first met, he took me along to a couple of games. I immediately got the bug.

‘So, when the demise happened, you felt it. This thing that was so important to you was suddenly gone. It was heartbreaking. The season after it happened, you’d bump into people wandering around the shopping centre because that was the only place left to go.’

As Scottish football carried on without them, a group of fans formed a collective called the United Clydebank Supporters and recovered the club name and crest from Airdrie United. ‘At that point,’ recalls McGibbon, ‘we basically had to take a crash course in how to run a football club. People talk about starting again from scratch. That’s what this was. Absolute scratch.’

Scottish football icon Davie Cooper started and finished his playing career with the Bankies

Item one on the agenda was an application to join the Scottish Junior Football League. After that was accepted, and after a year out of the game, Clydebank returned in time for the start of the 2003-04 campaign. Club legend Billy ‘Budgie’ McGhee was named manager, a new home at Glenhead Park in Duntocher was secured, and an improbable new chapter began.

Fast-forward roughly a quarter of a century, and the progress made is quite remarkable. Via various rungs of the former Scottish Junior Football Association and ground-hopping arrangements, Clydebank joined the West of Scotland League – the sixth tier of the Scottish football pyramid – in 2020. In 2024-25, they won promotion to the Lowland League West to move to within a step of a sensational return to the Scottish football league.

Win the league and they will go into a three-way, end-of-season play-off with the champions of Lowland League East and the Highland League. The winner of that round-robin will advance to a two-legged, home-and-away play-off against the team finishing bottom of SPFL League Two, sometimes referred to as ‘Club 42’. Win that tie and you’re playing League Two football next season.

‘We have a three-year plan to be in League Two,’ says McGibbon. ‘Within five years, League One. And after that, who knows? The most important thing is that we remain sustainable and fan-owned.

‘We can’t sell out to a big money man. Do that and you sell the soul of the club. I know because we’ve been there before. We can never again be in a position where one person has sole ownership of this club. It just can’t happen.’

Which raises the question of governance. The ten-person board, chaired by McGibbon, is entirely voluntary. ‘We don’t take a penny out of the club,’ she insists. ‘No expenses, nothing.’

Pop group Wet Wet Wet sponsored their hometown club Clydebank between 1993 and 1997

Another 30 or so volunteers manage various other parts of club business, from running the social media accounts to curating the matchday programme to operating the club shop. If it feels as though the community is showing up for its team, that’s because it is.

‘I think it harks back to the town’s working-class roots,’ says McGibbon. ‘And we try to embrace it in kind. We understand that it’s difficult for people to buy season tickets and such like with the cost of everything these days. That’s why we’ve put things in place to help, like payment plans. If we know someone genuinely can’t afford a ticket, we try to make it happen. Sometimes, it’s more important to have that person there than bringing in an extra few quid on the day.’

Crucially, the club has also invested in the Bronze Licence required for promotion into the upper tiers of the pyramid, a significant outlay that has the full backing of manager Gordon Moffat.

‘The whole trajectory of the club is so positive,’ he says. ‘For me, my coaches and the players, it’s really reassuring to see the way the club is run. Grace and the board are basically lifelong fans and it’s obvious to anyone they’ve got the club’s long-term future at heart.

‘When I came in seven years ago, I said to Grace that we’d need to increase the playing budget if we wanted to be competitive and, to her credit, she’s managed to do that whilst keeping us on a sure footing. She’s not scared to say no but, at the same time, she’s a fan and she wants to watch a good team.’

Clydebank chair Grace McGibbon is proud of the way the club has battled through adversity

Currently, that team includes an eclectic mix of joiners, electricians, engineers, firefighters, a barber and more. There’s a potent mix of youth and experience, with leaders in every position. Nicky Low, for example. The former Aberdeen and Dundee midfielder joined the Bankies in February 2023, back when they were still in the West of Scotland Football League.

‘I knew a few boys who were there at the time,’ says the 34-year-old. ‘I said to them, “Listen, is it professional the way it’s run, because I’m not coming if it’s a bag of washing”. Honestly, they couldn’t have spoken more highly of the place, and they were right to.

‘It’s the volunteer aspect that really gets me. Clydebank’s lucky that a lot of people give up their free time to help out, and you see what it means to them when you win and they’re all high-fiving you. Just seeing people smiling at football is what makes it all worthwhile.’

For Low, playing for Clydebank also represents something of a ‘full circle’ moment. ‘I was brought up in Greenock,’ he says, ‘so when Clydebank were ground-sharing with Morton back in the day, I was their ball boy. I’ve had a soft spot for them since I was a kid.’

All of which is lovely but football – as we are constantly reminded – is a results business, and Low is determined to continue Clydebank’s momentum with a win over Alloa in the Challenge Cup.

‘We’re under no illusions about how difficult a game it’s going to be,’ he says. ‘Alloa are a strong team. They play good football and Andy Graham will have them well organised. They’ll be favourites but we’ll go in believing that if we can bring the best version of ourselves, we’ll have a chance of progressing.

Holm Park will play host to a cup clash against Alloa that could provide a real fairytale

‘As a team and as individuals, we’re playing well and we always believe we can score, so if we can keep it tight at the back, I believe we’re capable of giving anybody a game.’

Manager Moffat agrees. ‘We’ve shown against League One and League Two teams over the last few seasons that we can compete. People will say, “It’s a one-off game, anything can happen.” But we’ve got a decent sample size in our favour now. Sure, we’ll lose some games to SPFL opposition, but I think we’ve proven we’re more than capable of winning plenty, too.’

As for McGibbon, she’s mostly just happy to have her team back. ‘I work in retail,’ she says. ‘Monday to Thursday. Nothing exciting. My passion comes from this football club, from the people, the fans, the coaches, the players. Every single person at the club, I absolutely love them for what they’ve given. That’s what makes it all worthwhile. I mean, you wouldn’t do this if it didn’t mean something to you. But it does. It’s very special.’

And who knows? Maybe one day there will be space on the wall for a photo of the team that restores Clydebank to the Scottish football league. They, too, will have earned their place.

■ Clydebank FC face Alloa Athletic in the last 32 of the KDM Evolution Trophy at Holm Park on Tuesday, November 3. Kick-off 7.45pm.

#1638. Charlton Athletic vs Sheffield United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 05 Nov 2026 22:29

Aiming to continue their climb up the Championship table and break into the playoff places, Sheffield United will head to The Valley to take on Charlton Athletic on Saturday.

Back-to-back victories have seen the visitors move within a point of the top eight, while their visitors sit four points above the drop zone after four straight losses.

Charlton Athletic return to action at the weekend aiming to end a dismal run of Championship form and arrest a drop towards the relegation zone.

Following a 19th-placed finish in their first season back in the second tier last time around, the Addicks won their first three league matches of the new term but have since drawn five and lost six of 11 matches.

In those games, Nathan Jones's side have scored just six goals and conceded 20, dropping to 21st spot in the process, just one place and four points above Burnley in the drop zone.

They have now suffered four straight defeats heading into their final match before the international break, falling to Watford, Norwich City and Middlesbrough before they hosted newly-promoted Bolton Wanderers on Tuesday and again came away empty-handed as Sam Dalby scored the only goal inside 20 minutes at the Valley.

With pressure surely growing on Jones, and the international break arguably coming at a decent time to arrest Charlton's slump, they will be desperate to put a win on the board to increase their lead over the drop zone ahead of the return to action.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to London aiming to carry an upturn in form into the break.

Unlike the hosts, Sheffield United are now bouncing back from a slow start to the Championship season, having set out to challenge for promotion this term only to pick up just nine points from their first eight matches before the opening break of the season.

Chris Wilder's men have reversed their fortunes since, though, putting 13 more points on the board in six outings courtesy of four wins and a draw alongside a solitary away defeat to Portsmouth.

Following a 1-0 home victory over Wrexham on Friday, the Blades headed to strugglers Preston North End on Tuesday and came from 1-0 down to win 3-2 thanks to Sydie Peck's first-half hat-trick, leaving them on 22 points from 14 matches with just five teams conceding fewer than the 17 goals they have allowed.

Now in a much better position in ninth spot, and just one point behind eighth-placed West Ham United, Sheffield United will look to make it three straight wins with the chance to head into the second break of the campaign in the playoff places.

Charlton Athletic remain unable to call on winger Rob Apter, who has been sidelined since early September.

In their midweek defeat, Jones replaced midfielder Nathaniel Chalobah with attacker Miles Leaburn at half time and could go with a more attacking shape from the outset at the weekend with Leaburn, Matt Godden, Sonny Carey and Millenic Alli all competing for attacking spots.

That is after Charlie Kelman led the line against Bolton with support from Harvey Knibbs, Karlan Grant and top scorer Tyreece Campbell, while Conor Coventry is a mainstay in the engine room and Will Mannion was preferred in net over Arthur Okonkwo last time out.

Sheffield United are without forwards Patrick Bamford and Ryan One and midfielder Joe Rothwell, while Kalvin Phillips was also absent in midweek but may be fit to feature.

He is unlikely to be rushed back, though, and Wilder should field a similar starting XI from their midweek away win, meaning Jairo Riedewald may again partner Peck, who decided that game with his hat-trick, while Liam Kitching should come straight back into the defence after serving a one-match suspension on Tuesday.

In a 4-4-2 shape, they may again be flanked by Romelle Donovan and Tahith Chong with Ben Brereton Diaz, Tom Cannon, Tyrese Campbell and Oliver Arblaster competing for attacking spots in Bamford's absence.

#1636. Opinion: Andoni Iraola finds perfect midfielder for Liverpool, it's not Lamine Camara

Liverpool's midfield has received some mixed reviews this season.

Before the 2026-27 season kicked off, fans felt like new midfielders should be the first thing on Liverpool's priority list.

However, for one reason or another, that didn't end up being the case with the Reds actually making their midfield weaker by allowing Curtis Jones to exit Anfield and join Inter Milan.

Obviously, Liverpool's lack of depth in the middle of the park has meant that James McConnell and Trey Nyoni have both been handed more regular roles but, since they're both so young, the Reds could still do with adding a new central midfielder to their ranks.

And now, the perfect option for them to explore may have just emerged.

Liverpool are preparing an £83 million offer for Federico Valverde

Alexis Mac Allister has easily been Liverpool's best central midfielder this season.

Last term, that was a completely different story with fans demanding that the Argentinian was moved on this summer due to how poorly he performed.

However, after the 2026 World Cup, something just seemed to click for the 27-year-old and he returned back to his best.

But, since his contract is going to expire in June 2028 and no renewal is in sight, change is clearly afoot.

So, this latest update from Fichajes about the Reds' interest in Federico Valverde should certainly pique the interest of fans.

"Liverpool are interested in signing Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde and are preparing a €100 million offer to secure his transfer in the upcoming summer transfer window," they wrote.

"Liverpool's primary target is a midfielder who can fill the void left by Alexis Mac Allister."

Federico Valverde would solve a lot of Liverpool's issues

Many different midfielders such as Lamine Camara have been linked with Liverpool recently.

And, while those rumours have stayed consistent, there's no hiding from the fact that Valverde would be a much better option for the Reds to explore.

Not only does he have a tonne of Champions League experience but, he's also been a part of one of football's best-ever teams for a number of years.

Obviously, the £83 million that Liverpool are willing to offer Real Madrid for Valverde's services may not be enough but, if it is, it would be money well spent.

His natural position is in the middle of the park but, Jose Mourinho has also used him as a right-back on several occasions this term.

Valverde's versatility, coupled with the experience he has make him a more or less perfect player for the Reds to target.

#1635. Opinion: Wonderkid will replace Liverpool veteran, he'll score goals

Liverpool's academy has always produced some top class talent.

Whether it's Steven Gerrard, Trent Alexander-Arnold or Curtis Jones, a lot of the Reds' academy graduates have played a regular role in the Reds' starting XI.

There have obviously been times when it's felt like things just aren't going their way but, with Andoni Iraola now at the helm, anything is possible.

Lewis Koumas, Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni have all been given consistent roles in the Spaniard's squad.

So, it only makes sense that one of the Reds' veterans is now going to be replaced by a wonderkid.

Jayden Danns will replace Federico Chiesa in Liverpool's squad

At this moment in time, it's unclear what Liverpool's plans for the January transfer window are going to be.

Some people believe that they have an idea of what's going to happen but, until it actually occurs, questions will arise.

Many players have been linked with joining and leaving Liverpool with a complete overhaul even being thrown into the ring at one point.

However, with Tribuna now confirming that the Reds are willing to let Federico Chiesa leave in January on a loan with an €8m-€10m option to buy, it's clear that change is already starting to occur.

"Inter are considering a move for Liverpool winger Federico Chiesa as they look to add a fifth forward to their squad in the January transfer window," they wrote.

"According to Tribuna.com sources, the Italian winger is emerging as one of the options being considered by the Nerazzurri. Chiesa has struggled for regular playing time at Liverpool and could be open to returning to Serie A.

"Liverpool would be willing to discuss a loan deal with an option to buy, with the permanent transfer fee set at around €8-10 million."

Jayden Danns would be the perfect successor for Federico Chiesa at Liverpool

As mentioned, Chiesa hasn't played all that much football over the last couple of years.

Most fans thought that his £10 million move back in August 2024 was going to be the bargain of the century.

And, even though he was mainly brought in to be Mohamed Salah's back-up, he was never really given the opportunity to fully prove his worth.

This then leads us to today, where, almost three years on, he's arguably in a worse position than he was before he joined Liverpool.

Losing Chiesa would obviously put Liverpool an attacker down but, with players such as Jayden Danns ready and waiting to be called up, it feels like they should be fine.

Danns is more of a striker than he is a winger but, with how many wingers Liverpool have among their ranks at the moment, they're probably more in need of a number nine.

That is, especially since Hugo Ekitike is still side-lined.

In the future, that could obviously change and a winger might end up being more needed but, right now, if Chiesa does go in January, Danns is literally the perfect replacement for the Italian.

This extra chance to feature for Liverpool's first-team could be massive for his confidence and his progression which is why, especially with Iraola at the helm, bringing Danns in to succeed Chiesa makes total sense.

By Joshua Ojele | 05 Nov 2026 22:31, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 22:49

Minnesota United and San Jose Earthquakes draw the curtain on their 2026 Major League Soccer regular season campaign when they lock horns at Allianz Field on Sunday morning.

While the home side head into the league finale needing maximum points to stand a chance of securing back-to-back playoff appearances, San Jose will aim to finish the campaign strong and gather momentum ahead of the post-season quest.

A strong showing at the business end of the season has put Minnesota United in contention for playoff qualification ahead of a crunch final-day showdown, with the Loons securing a 3-1 win over Los Angeles FC on Monday to maintain their newfound form.

Joaquin Pereyra turned in an eye-catching display at the BMO Stadium, netting on either side of Cherrion Valerius’s 34th-minute strike to put the visitors three goals up, before Sergio Vasquez pulled one back for Los Angeles FC in the 89th minute.

Coming off a 3-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City on October 29, Minnesota United have now picked up three wins in their most recent four outings and are unbeaten in six straight matches (3W 3D), having lost each of the five games preceding this run.

This late-season resurgence has seen Cameron Knowles’s men surge into 12th place in the Western Conference standings with 41 points from 33 matches, just two points behind ninth-placed Colorado Rapids in the final playoff qualifying spot.

Attacking improvements have been integral in Minnesota’s upturn in form, with 2+ goals scored in five of their last six games, and they will also hope to make home advantage count against an opposing side who have failed to win their last six league visits to Allianz Field, losing four and claiming two draws since a 3-1 victory in May 2018.

Having seen their form take a dip in recent weeks, San Jose Earthquakes finally rediscovered their winning touch last Saturday when they held on to see out a 2-1 victory over Real Salt Lake and record their first victory since late September.

In an action-packed first half at PayPal Park, Ousseni Bouda and Benjamin Kikanovic netted in a 15-minute spell to put the Quakes in a commanding lead, and after Juan Sanabria halved the deficit with a 23rd-minute strike, the home side did well to repel Real Salt Lake and leave with all three points.

Prior to that, San Jose saw their nine-game unbeaten league streak come to an end on October 25, when they were hammered 3-0 by FC Dallas at the Toyota Stadium, four days before playing out a 2-2 stalemate with Colorado Rapids on home turf.

After enduring a disappointing 2025 campaign that saw them finish 10th in the West and narrowly miss out on the playoffs, Bruce Arena’s men have enjoyed a significant turnaround this season, collecting 52 points from 33 games to sit third in the conference standings, three points behind second-placed Dallas.

With playoff qualification already assured, San Jose will be keen to finish the regular season on a high, but a run of just one win in eight matches since August suggests they still have work to do before the campaign concludes.

San Jose Earthquakes Major League Soccer form:

American youngster Kayne Rizvanovich was left out of the team list against Los Angeles FC last time out, and the 19-year-old goalkeeper is also expected to sit out this weekend's matchup.

Kelvin Yeboah has been a standout performer for Minnesota this season, and the Italian striker, who has racked up 18 goals and four assists in 29 league starts, will be one to keep an eye on.

#1632. Report: Liverpool start talks for biggest signing of 2027 - it's the talk of the transfer window

Liverpool have reportedly started initial talks for the biggest signing of 2027. This will be the talk of the transfer window.

Liverpool made absolutely no waves in the 2024 transfer windows. Zero waves. They did, essentially, nothing at all.

Now didn't that change in 2025? Liverpool went on to break their transfer record twice in that summer, including the overall British transfer record as they signed Alexander Isak from Newcastle United.

Even more money went out in 2026. Liverpool signed Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola for well over £200m as the squad revamp continued at pace.

All eyes now turn to 2027 as we wait and see what Liverpool do. There's, in theory, less of a need for big signings after the last couple of years, while the Reds have a new sporting director in Julian Ward who, historically anyway, does things differently.

And yet, they may actually be moving towards the most notable signing of 2027.

Cadena SER reports that Liverpool have been in contact about a possible January move for Trent Alexander-Arnold. The Scouser is now third choice right-back at Real Madrid and it’s believed they’d be willing to do some sort of deal this winter.

However, it would likely be a loan deal with things potentially moving forward from there.

And it’s one that makes sense. Real Madrid aren’t playing him, Alexander-Arnold needs to play, and Liverpool do not have a right-back they’re happy with. If not for the obvious history, this would be an incredibly suitable deal for all parties that would naturally be explored.

But there is that history. Alexander-Arnold did not leave on good terms and going back to Anfield would be admitting defeat, essentially. It’ll even feel like that from the Liverpool point of view - an admittance that they couldn’t find a right-back to replace him.

The thing is, though, both angles are true. Liverpool have not found a right-back to replace him and were never going to. Alexander-Arnold has failed at Real Madrid and looks increasingly unlikely to break through there.

So for both parties, this all makes sense. Again, if not for the history, Liverpool would be all over such a deal and we imagine Alexander-Arnold would be, too.

This would be one of the biggest and most notable transfers of 2027. Maybe even the biggest, such was Alexander-Arnold’s level at Liverpool. The return of one of the world’s best.

Dallas and Colorado Rapids will look to close out the 2026 MLS regular season campaign on a strong note when they go head to head in the season finale at the Toyota Stadium on Sunday morning.

Both sides head into the game having something to play for, with the hosts in a two-man race with San Jose Earthquakes for second place in the Western Conference standings, while Colorado will be aiming to seal their spot in the playoffs.

Having finished 11th and seventh in the 2024 and 2025 MLS seasons respectively, Dallas have taken another significant step forward this term and are closing in on their highest conference finish since their 2016 title triumph.

With just eight clean sheets and 50 goals conceded in the league, improvements must be made at the back ahead of their post-season campaign, but Eric Quill’s men can take pride in their performance at the attacking end of the pitch, where they have netted a club record 56 goals so far.

Dallas' defensive shortcomings were on display last Saturday when they were held to a 1-1 draw by Sporting Kansas City at Children's Mercy Park, with Jansen Miller netting a 45th-minute equaliser to cancel out Herman Johansson’s 19th-minute opener and force a share of the spoils.

Having suffered a 2-1 defeat against Columbus Crew at the Toyota Stadium last Thursday, the Bulls have now dropped five points in their last two matches, with their recent dip in form dealing a significant blow to their hopes of securing the conference title.

Dallas head into the season finale with 15 wins and 10 draws from their 33 MLS matches to collect 55 points and sit second in the Western Conference standings, six points adrift of first-placed Vancouver Whitecaps.

Like the host, a slump in form at the business end of the season has threatened to derail Colorado Rapids’ campaign, with Matt Wells’s men dropping three more points in a 4-2 home defeat at the hands of Chicago Fire last Sunday.

Second-half strikes from Robert Lewandowski, Puso Dithejane, and a brace from Jonathan Bamba inspired Chicago Fire to all three points at Dick's Sporting Goods Park, with Morgan Whittaker and Paxten Aaronson getting on the scoresheet for the home side.

Colorado Rapids have their fair share of injury concerns, with 28-year-old defender Reggie Cannon and the Ghanaian duo of Ali Fadal and Ibrahim Sadiq all ruled out of this weekend matchup.
