The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Old Trafford and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

As we speak, there have just been two goals scored in the last few moments in the two early kick-offs. Both home sides, Fenerbahce and PSV, have just equalised in their respective games.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1602. 'We owe it to Michael Carrick': Kobbie Mainoo lays down the gauntlet for his Man United team-mates - and claims they are just ONE win away from transforming their season

Published: 10:37 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EDT, 2 November 2026

Kobbie Mainoo says Manchester United’s stars owe it to head coach Michael Carrick and the fans to turn their season around – and believe it might only take one win.

United go into Tuesday’s Champions League tie against Roma at Old Trafford without a victory in nine games and hovering one place above the Premier League relegation zone.

It has left Carrick fighting for his job and led to fans turning on the players after the last home game against Bournemouth which ended with a 3-0 defeat.

Carrick has done his best to shield the squad from criticism, and Mainoo said: ‘I feel like our way to repay that is to also be behind the manager on the pitch and off it, and fight for us as a team.

‘In these tough times you can't expect the fans 100,000 per cent of the time to be happy and cheering when we're not putting out results, you know. We owe it to them to put the results out there for them to cheer again.

‘Of course, it's been a tough season. We've not had the results we've wanted, but you know we need to look forward now. There are big, big games ahead and I feel like we're one win away from changing that.

Kobbie Mainoo says Manchester United’s stars owe it to Michael Carrick and the fans to turn their season around

‘I've been at this club for a long time and I know there's always going to be ups and downs. It's never going to be plain sailing and smooth to the top. So you expect bumps and the best thing about them is you're able to bounce back from them.’

Mainoo signed a new five-year contract in April after re-establishing himself at his boyhood club under Carrick, having asked to leave under the previous head coach Ruben Amorim.

Despite the club’s fortunes taking a nosedive this season, the 21-year-old is determined to help restore the standards that made United great.

‘I'm very grateful to the boss for putting the trust in me as soon as he came in, putting that belief in me and giving me all the advice that he has,’ added Mainoo, who returned to action at Chelsea on Saturday after missing five games.

‘Knowing he's a player who's been at this club and knows the history of this club and knows what it takes to win, I take those words to heart and I try and apply them every day in training and in games.

‘United's a huge club, so I think a lot of people know the values that this club holds and that have been passed down through the people who've worked and played here. I feel like I take some responsibility in that and in spreading the word of what is Manchester United, coming up through the academy. I plan to send that message for hopefully as long as I can.

‘I've tried to take on more responsibility in the team. I want to impose myself more in games and they've definitely helped to do that, giving me more responsibility with taking the ball. There have been ups and downs, but I have to have belief in myself even in these tough times.

‘I feel like in every period of my career so far, I've tried to take positives from them. Even, you know, times that I'm not playing I've learned things and I'm still applying them to this day.’

#1601. Report: Is Liverpool player actually good enough? Club is torn

One club is torn on a Liverpool star. Is he actually good enough to justify the money involved?

Alisson Becker's future is up in the air. We certainly don't know what's going to happen with him and we're not sure Liverpool do, either.

His contract expires at the end of the season, of course. It was due to expire last summer but Liverpool triggered a clause that extended things another year. Even with that, speculation that Allisson could join Juventus ran rampant and it's certainly true that the Old Lady pushed to sign the player.

But Alisson stuck around and it's a good thing, too. He remains Liverpool's best goalkeeper and by some distance - if he does leave, the club is up against it to sign someone to even maintain the standards, let alone improve them.

Which is why it's quite strange that a potential destination for Alisson isn't even convinced about signing him.

Alisson Becker's futureAlisson has been linked with a few clubs but two in particular: Juventus and Flamengo. Flamengo, the biggest club in Brazil, feel best-placed to get him back in his native country. However, Sport Witness claim the Brazilians aren’t sure Alisson is actually good enough to justify a move. They cite his performances for the national team as evidence that he’s not the elite-level goalkeeper that many think he is. That, of course, is completely insane. Alisson has won everything at club level and any Liverpool fan who remembers that last few decades would say he’s by far the best goalkeeper the club has had since the formation of the Premier League.

Alisson has been linked with a few clubs but two in particular: Juventus and Flamengo. Flamengo, the biggest club in Brazil, feel best-placed to get him back in his native country.

That, of course, is completely insane. Alisson has won everything at club level and any Liverpool fan who remembers that last few decades would say he’s by far the best goalkeeper the club has had since the formation of the Premier League.

So we’re in a situation where Alisson may not quite have the offers that many thought he would. Does that change things for Liverpool?

There’s surely a scenario here where paying to renew Alisson’s deal makes sense and a lack of competition will naturally drive his wage demands down. We still believe Liverpool will move on because of his age but the natural difficulty in replacing him must keep the door open to a new deal in some respect.

Flamengo fumbling their position makes it easier for Liverpool to do that.

#1600. Alverca vs Casa Pia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 05 Nov 2026 23:29

Alverca will be looking to avoid a fourth consecutive defeat in all competitions when they welcome Casa Pia to the Complexo Desportivo FC Alverca on Saturday evening for their Liga Portugal Matchday 11 encounter.

Sergio Ferreira's side sit 10th in the Primeira Liga table, four points and six places above their visitors, who currently occupy one of the two outright relegation spots.

Alverca's second consecutive campaign in the Portuguese top flight has been characterised by spells of inconsistency, with a three-match winning run against Nacional, Rio Ave and Famalicao between mid-September and October sandwiched between winless periods.

Ferreira's men had failed to win any of their opening five fixtures before finding their feet, but they have since returned to familiar struggles after losing their last three outings without scoring, beginning with a Taca de Portugal elimination at the hands of lower-league Tondela before suffering successive 1-0 league losses to Arouca and Benfica.

Looking to avoid a third consecutive defeat in the top-flight for the first time since December 2025, the Ribatejo outfit must also find greater balance at both ends of the pitch, having scored 13 goals and conceded 14 in 10 Primeira Liga matches, with multiple strikes coming just once and only one clean sheet recorded during that period.

Alverca’s home form has offered little encouragement either, as Ferreira's side have managed just one victory in five matches on their own turf this season (D2, L2), with their most recent outing at the venue ending in defeat to Arouca.

The hosts can nevertheless draw some confidence from previous results in this fixture, having won both league meetings with the Geese last season, recording a 2-0 victory in Rio Maior before following it up with a 3-1 success on home soil in April.

Casa Pia find themselves in a similarly difficult position after finishing 16th last season and securing their top-flight status through the relegation playoff, with their disappointing start to the current campaign largely down to shortcomings at both ends of the pitch.

Filipe Coelho's men have scored a joint-league-low five goals in the Primeira Liga this term, while only Maritimo (20) and Rio Ave (23) have conceded more than Os Gansos' 19, with their lack of cutting edge in attack once again evident in last weekend's 2-0 defeat to Sporting Lisbon.

There are, however, signs of improvement compared to their opening six fixtures, during which the Geese went without a victory, having now won two of their last four league matches and three of their most recent five across all competitions, including a Taca de Portugal triumph over lower-league Alpendorada.

A return to the road this weekend could also work in the visitors' favour, considering all seven of their league points this season have come away from home, with those results arriving across their last three trips, including a 2-0 victory over Estrela Amadora on their most recent outing.

Alverca remain without Bastien Meupiyou and Sabit Abdulai, who are both sidelined through injury, while goalkeeper Jhonatan Luiz and midfielder Rayan Lucas are doubts after completing modified training sessions earlier this week.

Steven Baseya and Andre Vidigal are available again after serving their respective suspensions, providing Ferreira with two additional options as he considers his selection for Saturday's encounter.

For Casa Pia, goalkeeper Andre Gomes appears to be the only confirmed absentee, while Jeremy Livolant is pushing for a starting place after playing 45 minutes against Sporting.

David Sousa is also one booking away from suspension, having collected four yellow cards this season, and another caution on Saturday would rule him out of the Taca de Portugal fourth-round meeting with Atletico CP on November 21.

Henrique Araujo could retain his place as the central striker, although Coelho also has Alasanna Jatta and veteran forward Cassiano available as alternative options.

Alverca have struggled to find the net in recent weeks, while their home record offers little reason to expect a convincing response, particularly against opponents who have collected all their league points on their travels this season.

Casa Pia have also lacked consistency in front of goal, but their recent away performances suggest that they are capable of making life difficult for the hosts, and a closely fought draw could be on the cards.

#1597. RB Leipzig vs Augsburg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 05 Nov 2026 23:32, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:12

Desperate to end their Bundesliga slump, Augsburg will travel to face RB Leipzig at Red Bull Arena on Saturday.

Die Roten Bullen are hoping to bounce back from their midweek defeat, with Die Fuggerstadter winless in six league games.

Martin Demichelis's Leipzig currently sit fourth in the German top flight with 15 points to their name, just three shy of Borussia Dortmund and leaders Bayern Munich.

The Saxons have also been flawless in the league at Red Bull Arena, where they are yet to concede in domestic competition, not to mention that only Bayern have bettered their 22-goal tally in the Bundesliga so far.

However, Demichelis is facing intense criticism from the media in Leipzig, who have directly questioned the manager's position, prompting him to state that if he does not achieve the club's aims then he will leave of his own accord at the end of the season.

Former Roten Bullen boss Marco Rose - now of Bournemouth - also spoke out about the level of pressure on Demichelis, noting that, "If you know the media landscape a bit, you already get the feeling that the thumbs are down."

The Cherries' head coach then went on to reveal how the end of his tenure at Red Bull Arena "Did something" to him, and caused him to lose a bit of his "Lightness."

Last time out, Leipzig were beaten 3-2 by Manchester City in a Champions League thriller, bringing a three-game winning streak to an end, and marking the first time the hosts conceded on home turf this season.

Victory this weekend would be a fourth in five matches for Demichelis, and may even put Die Roten Bullen level with Dortmund and Bayern, though another defeat is likely to trigger a new wave of criticism.

Meanwhile, Manuel Baum's Augsburg kicked off their season in strong fashion with back-to-back triumphs, but have since endured a dire winless run in the Bundesliga.

Die Fuggerstatder last took all three points by thrashing Eintracht Frankfurt 4-1 on September 6, losing three and drawing three of their league games since.

The only bright spot during that stretch was a 4-2 DFB-Pokal success against Grossaspach, though it was followed up by a 2-1 defeat to Freiburg at WWK Arena just four days later.

Heading into Saturday's showdown, Augsburg are 10th in the Bundesliga with nine points, putting them just one shy of the top half but level with every club down to 15th-placed Hamburger SV, and only two points above Union Berlin in the relegation playoff spot.

This weekend's visitors will arrive as the underdogs, but the more optimistic amongst the travelling support could take heart from the fact Baum's side have earned three of their four wins across all competitions away from home.

Leipzig will be without striker Marc Guiu once again as he recovers from a hamstring injury, while winger Antonio Nusa is a doubt after being substituted against Man City as a precautionary measure, with manager Demichelis saying that the 21-year-old "Was close to getting injured."

Nusa could start on the left of the Saxons' attack this weekend, but if he is not ready to feature, then Tidiam Gomis could take his place in the XI.

Elsewhere, left-back Max Finkgrafe is a doubt with a thigh issue, and midfielder Assan Ouedraogo remains sidelined due to a shoulder injury.

In their absence, David Raum should start on the left of the Saxons' defence, while Neil El Aynaoui and Rocco Reitz operate in Leipzig's double pivot.

As for Augsburg, they are light at the back given that centre-halves Noahkai Banks (knee), Calvin Brackelmann (concussion) and Abdulai Juma Bah (suspension) are all unavailable.

Filling the gaps, Baum could opt for Jeffrey Gouweleeuw, Yannik Keitel and Chrislain Matsima to form his defence, with Robin Fellhauer and Hennes Behrens as wing-backs.

Vandevoordt; Henrichs, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; El Aynaoui, Reitz; Gomis, Nkunku, Nusa; Romulo

Dahmen; Gouweleeuw, Keitel, Matsima; Fellhauer, Massengo, Rieder, Behrens; Kade, Ibrahimovic; Gregoritsch

Leipzig may have been beaten by Man City in midweek, but their record at Red Bull Arena speaks for itself, and they should be able to get the better of their struggling opponents on Saturday.

Augsburg will be desperate for a win this weekend, yet they arrive as significant underdogs against a team that have not conceded on home turf in the league.

#1594. DC United vs New York City FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 05 Nov 2026 23:38, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 23:44

DC United and New York City FC bring the curtain down on their respective 2026 Major League Soccer campaigns with Saturday's clash at Audi Field.

With playoff football out of reach for both sides, there is little at stake, but the chance to finish the regular season on a high should ensure a respectable level of intent.

After reaching the postseason in each of the last two years, New York City have only themselves to blame for missing out this term, following a dismal run of just two wins from 15 outings since returning from Leagues Cup duty.

Pascal Jansen’s men would have gone into their season finale still in playoff contention with a win over Montreal - a result they looked set to secure thanks to Andres Perea’s opener - before Daniel Rios stunned Citi Field with a 91st-minute equaliser.

That was the 12th of 45 goals conceded by the Pigeons between the 75th minute and full time, a lack of late-game focus that Jansen must address next season, should he remain in charge.

While largely inconsequential, a win over DC United could marginally bolster the 57-year-old’s prospects of staying in the dugout, but his record against Saturday’s opposite number is poor, with two defeats from their previous two managerial head-to-heads.

Having lost each of the last two editions - one to this weekend’s opponents - NYCFC’s recent record in season finales is underwhelming as this weekend’s visitors seek to hand DC United a first defeat in five meetings.

As DC United prepare to close out their 2026 MLS campaign, they will hope never to endure another season as disappointing as this one, which easily ranks among the worst in the club’s history since returning to the top flight in 2008.

February’s 1-0 triumph over Philadelphia Union was expected to signal the start of something special for Rene Weiler’s men, but they have since suffered a downward spiral - not quite as severe as last season’s bottom-place finish in the Eastern Conference, but still disappointing.

Saturday’s 3-0 defeat to Columbus Crew marked a fifth consecutive loss and a 14th in 33 matches for Rene Weiler’s side, who have managed just seven wins this term, the second-fewest in the division, ahead of only Montreal’s tally of six.

With just 39 goals scored, the Eagles have been largely ineffective at the top end of the pitch despite Tai Baribo’s impressive return of 16 goals in 25 matches, without which things would have looked much worse from an attacking perspective.

Weiler’s 0.95 points per game in charge of DC United is his lowest average across all clubs managed since 2019. While his position appears safe for now, the Swiss coach will already be planning a turnaround next season, and avoiding defeat on Saturday would at least offer a positive note to end an otherwise disastrous campaign.

New York City FC Major League Soccer form:

Hosei Kijima and Louis Munteanu remain sidelined with leg injuries, while Gabriel Segal is unavailable for DC United due to an ankle problem.

First-choice goalkeeper Sean Johnson (knee) remains out, so Alex Bono should continue between the posts.

Top scorer Tai Baribo will not have the chance to add to his 16 goals due to a hip problem, rounding out the hosts’ list of absentees alongside Kye Rowles, who misses out through suspension.

New York City’s Australian duo Kai Trewin and Aiden O’Neill are out with ankle injuries, while fellow midfielder Maxi Moralez (knee) continues his spell on the treatment table.

Nineteen-year-old Drew Baiera has seen his debut campaign disrupted by injuries and will not feature this weekend, joining Arnau Farnos (leg) and Alonso Martinez (thigh) on the sidelines.

An entertaining contest with both sides going full throttle is expected, but we are backing Jansen’s men to come out on top.

#1593. Crystal Palace determined to keep ‘key’ player as new contract talks continue

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Crystal Palace are reportedly determined to keep Ismaïla Sarr beyond the January transfer window, with discussions over a new contract offering fresh hope that the winger will remain at Selhurst Park.

The Senegal international attracted significant attention during the summer, including reported interest from Liverpool and Galatasaray.

Although Palace rejected approaches for the 28-year-old, questions have continued over his future following a difficult start to the season.

According to ⁠Football Insider, Palace have held positive discussions with Sarr over a potential contract extension and are hopeful of reaching an agreement.

The club reportedly view the winger as an important part of manager Pierre Sage’s plans and are reluctant to consider offers in January.

That stance follows a summer in which Liverpool reportedly made an offer worth around £50 million for Sarr. Palace ultimately kept hold of the forward, while interest from Turkey and the Saudi Pro League has continued.

A new contract could help Palace protect their position and discourage potential suitors from pursuing a move in the coming months. However, an agreement has not yet been confirmed.

Galatasaray remain one of the clubs to watch, having reportedly made an approach for Sarr during the summer transfer window.

Football Insider reports that the Turkish club could revisit their interest in January, particularly if the winger continues to struggle for regular playing time at Palace.

Sarr has endured a slow start to the campaign and has also dealt with fitness issues. His limited involvement has fuelled speculation about his future, although Palace are reportedly not allowing his recent lack of minutes to change their longer-term plans.

Liverpool were also linked with a move during the summer, but a January transfer to Anfield remains uncertain.

#1592. GdS: Milan search for ‘spark’ in Europe – how Amorim plans to harness post-derby ‘fuel’

After beating Inter in the derby on Saturday night, AC Milan are hoping that they can ride the wave and get back on track in Europe.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Milan want to rediscover their ‘international DNA’ and put behind them a start to the Europa League campaign that has seen one win and two defeats in the first three games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

While it is not yet a do-or-die situation for Ruben Amorim and his squad, failing to secure a win against the Hungarian side – who have a perfect record so far – would make reaching the top 24 significantly more difficult, and a top-eight finish nearly impossible.

Given that the Rossoneri have won seven Champions League titles, no other team in this European competition can boast such a trophy cabinet. Furthermore, the Portuguese manager reached the final with Manchester United two editions ago, ultimately losing to Tottenham.

Consequently, Milan and Amorim must ‘honour’ the Europa League in a manner far removed from their last away outing, which was a heavy defeat against European debutants Bournemouth, with Mike Maignan getting sent off.

This evening over 50,000 fans are expected at San Siro, including a sold-out away sector of 4,200, with over 5,000 Hungarian fans in total throughout the stadium. Milan must secure a victory, channelling the enthusiasm currently felt at Milanello following Saturday’s derby win.

The former United manager tried to brush it aside so his squad could focus solely on the Europa League, but the atmosphere during the final training session was as upbeat as it gets, with lots of ‘slaps’ of congratulations dished out.

Koni De Winter was patted on the back in celebration of his daughter’s birth, Diego Moreira was praised for his goal in the derby, Sankhoun Diawara was acknowledged for his debut(s), and even coach Carlos Fernandes got some love for the corner routine leading to Adrien Rabiot’s goal.

😂 A lot of slaps were given out before training: De Winter for the birth of his daughter, Pulisic for his renewal, Diawara for his debut and Carlos Fernandes for the corner routine leading to Rabiot’s goal ❤️🖤

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 4, 2026

The enthusiasm following the derby must now be channelled into focus and determination ahead of the Europa League return. Milan cannot afford another embarrassing performance in European competition, like those seen against Benfica and Bournemouth.

The club’s storied history forbids it, and Gerry Cardinale certainly wouldn’t welcome a repeat of those displays against the Portuguese or English sides. For this reason, while rotating the squad with an eye on Sunday’s match in Genoa, Amorim will ensure the team retains some key pillars.

De Winter will remain in defence, Yunus Musah and Rabiot in midfield, and Goncalo Ramos in attack. Compared to Saturday’s lineup, there will be seven changes including a forced one in goal, with Lorenzo Torriani replacing the suspended Maignan. Ardon Jashari steps in for Luka Modrić, who will be rested.

With six players sidelined due to injury, the scope for rotation is limited. Yet, even while fielding a side with a significantly lower average age than the one that played in the derby (23.6 years versus 28.1), Amorim has opted not to throw 18-year-olds Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto into the XI.

His goal is to help Gonçalo Ramos – who hasn’t managed a single shot on target in his last two appearances – regain his scoring touch. Consequently, Camarda will have to wait a little longer. As for Comotto, the midfield requires experience, and both Rabiot and Musah are too vital to be left out.

Across the 2024-25 Champions League and the current Europa League campaign, the Rossoneri have won only one of their last six matches, hardly the kind of record expected from a club with such a storied continental past.

According to UEFA, a win in the Europa League is worth €450,000 (with €150,000 for a draw), figures that pale in comparison to the rewards for similar results in the Champions League (€2.1m and €700k, respectively).

The total earnings at the end of each competition are also incomparable: Champions League finalists can rake in between €120m and €125m, whereas the winner of the Europa League can earn, at most, just over €40m.

However, securing the second-tier European trophy guarantees direct qualification for the 2027-28 Champions League, bypassing the need to finish in the top four of Serie A. It also grants a spot in the UEFA Super Cup, which awards €4m to each of the two participating clubs.

Returning to the Champions League – a major objective that was not achieved last season – must be achieved this year, not least for the sake of sponsorships and brand value, two areas of great importance to Cardinale.

Ultimately, the goal is to win a trophy, ideally the Scudetto. However, adding the Europa League title to the trophy cabinet would certainly be a welcome achievement, especially given Milan didn’t win it when it was the UEFA Cup either.

#1591. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

#1590. Stephen Robinson proud of his battling Dons but injury crisis deepens

Published: 17:30 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 14:43 EDT, 2 November 2026

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson has revealed his injury crisis has become even more catastrophic ahead of the weekend league visit of Hibernian that has the potential to make or break his reign.

The Dons manager saw his side put in a fine, disciplined display in going down 1-0 to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup final, but lost Emmanuel Gyamfi within 15 minutes after he collided with Kim Min-su and also has Brad Lyons battling a knock.

Robinson admitted afterwards that there is no chance of longer-term absentees Chris Cadden, Mats Knoester and Lewis Mayo being available, with Dan Happe the only player likely to return for the Saturday night showdown with Premiership bottom dogs Hibs after being suspended last night.

‘Gyamfi will be out for a long period of time,’ reported Robinson. ‘It looked like it was maybe the other thigh that he’s had a problem with. It’s a heartbreaker for the boy.

‘Brad Lyons took a really bad knock. I’m not sure how serious that is. Hopefully, he’s got away with it.

‘Chris Cadden will be out for six weeks. Mats Knoester is four to six weeks.

Emmanuel Gyamfi limped off early with an injury in Aberdeen's semi-final defeat

‘The only plus point is Dan Happe. It’s very difficult because half the squad are not available. Any team that does well, there’s consistency and patience.

‘Over time, the last person that had prolonged success in Aberdeen was Derek (McInnes). He was given a lot of time and a lot of support, but we’ve not been able to put a consistent team, never mind a consistent shape, on the pitch.

‘It’s four changes every week at the moment.’

Robinson, however, stated his pride in the way his players performed and backed centre-back Jack Milne while taking a pop at the criticism he has come in for of late.

‘They rose against adversity this time. They put in a real performance,’ he said.

‘Rangers scored during our best spell in the game, which is unfortunate, but it’s been a tough week for us with injuries, really tough.

‘They showed great character and courage.

‘Jack’s a young man. Surprisingly, he’s from Aberdeen and he still gets an incredible amount of stick.

‘He’s had one full season and he’s a lovely boy that wants to learn. He’s just learning the game. I thought he showed real character.’

Dons boss Stephen Robinson on the touchline in the 1-0 defeat to Rangers

Robinson also refused to criticise captain Kevin Nisbet after seeing him pass up a couple of golden chances.

‘If you want chances to fall to anyone, it’s Kevin and he had the opportunity to play Mitchy Ntelo in with one of them when clean through,’ he reflected.

‘We had grown into the game. We were organised defensively despite not knowing what our team would be until Saturday morning.

‘I’m proud of the players because they gave me absolutely everything.

‘You’d need to ask the fans if they saw positive performances. I can only answer for myself. I saw a group of boys give everything in adversity.

‘Everyone expected us to roll over and get battered but that wasn’t the case. They’ve shown they have the character to play for Aberdeen in big games, no doubt.’

#1586. Ferencvaros boss Borbely ready to face ‘giant’ Milan with confidence: “Prepared for every eventuality”

Ferencvaros head coach Borbely Balazs insists that his side will come to San Siro and face AC Milan playing their way.

Having joined Ferencvaros from last season’s Hungarian title winners ETO Gyori, Balazs has made an excellent start to the campaign with his new club. They sit in third in their domestic league, two points off top but with a game in hand to be played.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

They have racked up 20 games unbeaten across all competitions, also winning three games out of three in the Europa League too. A 3-1 away win at Celtic was followed by home wins over Viktoria Plzen (2-1) and Torreense (4-1), making them one of the early pace-setters.

So, this is a big opportunity for the Fradi, who will be backed by around 5,000 away fans. The head coach of the Hungarian side – Borbely Balazs – spoke at a press conference last night at San Siro about tonight’s contest, and his words were relayed by MilanPress.

Do you remember your last time at San Siro?

“It’s been a long time: more than twenty years have passed since I was last lucky enough to play at San Siro. It’s a shame, however, that we had to play in front of empty stands back then.

“It was still a fantastic experience: we faced true world-class stars, like Materazzi, Adriano, and Luis Figo. Despite the four-goal defeat, it remains a fond memory.”

“I’m not someone who likes to look too far ahead. When the draw determined that we’d face both AC Milan and Juventus, I was struck by the fact that we were facing two giants of Italian football, clubs with immense traditions.

“It’s a truly special occasion! It’s difficult to predict how AC Milan will play, given that they frequently change their tactical system. They have several players out due to injury or suspension, and we know they rotate a lot, so we had a clear idea of ​​their starting line-up.

“However, we’ve prepared for every eventuality and arrived at San Siro with the right amount of confidence.”

“Our European campaign has been positive so far, but the match against Milan will be on a completely different level, even though we’ve faced strong opponents in recent months.

“The Rossoneri will likely retain possession more, so we’ll have to play with discipline, but we also need to be courageous when we attack.”

“My role model is Carlo Ancelotti. I’ve always followed the careers of Italian coaches. I’m Slovakian, and since several Slovakian players have played in Serie A, I’ve also kept an eye on their careers, as well as the coaches they’ve worked with.”

“It’s a source of great pride for all of us who represent Hungarian football.”

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

The comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton. He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”

For Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be important. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January plans. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

#1578. MN: 11 defeats in 20 for Allegri – why the Cagliari loss may have been a blessing for Milan

A report this morning has put forward the notion that it may be a blessing in disguise that AC Milan missed out on the Champions League.

MilanNews write that the club ‘have Cagliari to thank for that May day at San Siro’. It’s paradoxical, following an initial instinctive reaction: how can Milan hosting Ferencvaros be better than facing PSG, Barcelona ​​or Manchester City on a magical Champions League night?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Well, considering how Massimiliano Allegri is doing with Napoli, there is a compelling case that it was necessary pain. The report explained the thesis.

Allegri’s decline began on 15 March 2026, the day of the 1-0 defeat away against Lazio after he won the derby thanks to Pervis Estupinan’s goal. It takes us to 4 November 2026, the date of Porto 4-1 Napoli, that latest terrible result from the coach.

It seems that bad results constant tension in the dressing room have followed Max in the past few months. In this block of 20 matches between Milan and Napoli, Allegri’s difficulty is evident, with a decidedly negative record of 11 defeats against only six wins and three draws.

Furthermore, 31 goals conceded in 20 matches is enormous for teams historically led by a pragmatic and defensive manager like the Livorno-born manager. Essentially, since that derby won with that surreal goal from Estupinan, ‘Allegrismo’ has only meant disasters.

The feeling is that if Milan had celebrated their return to the Champions League they would have kept Allegri, but in the long run they would have wasted another year chasing a style of football and a way of managing the club that no longer seems viable.

Less than 24 hours after the Cagliari game, there was a clear-out of the management as Gerry Cardinale saw fit to launch yet another revolution. It takes time and patience, but perhaps it’s better this way, to feel like something is genuinely being built towards.

Without Giorgio Furlani as CEO, the club will be entrusted to a competent and experienced Head of Football (likely to be Markus Krösche, a director with obvious pedigree). With Ruben Amorim at the helm, we can expect to see a more modern and entertaining style.

There are of course inconsistencies to iron out, and the squad must be improved, but we must question what would have been lost had Cagliari not made history that night at San Siro.

#1576. Nacional vs Academico de Viseu - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 05 Nov 2026 23:44

Academico de Viseu will be out to secure their seventh league victory on the trot when they travel to Estadio da Madeira on Saturday to face a Nacional side still searching for stability following another managerial change.

The visitors sit sixth in the Liga Portugal table, just below the continental places on goal difference, while that same metric has the hosts 15th and only just clear of the relegation zone.

Nacional will hope that their third managerial appointment of the season can provide the stability needed to climb away from the lower reaches of the table following the arrival of Joao Henriques on October 26, after Alexandre Santos' brief spell in charge.

Santos suffered defeat in all four of his matches at the helm, including a shock Taca de Portugal exit to lower-league Sanjoanense, before Under-19s manager Bruno Abreu took charge and guided the side to a 1-0 victory over Braga, ending their six-match losing run in the league.

However, Henriques was unable to build on that result in his first game in charge, with the Alvinegros suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat away to Arouca, leaving the Funchal outfit with just two wins from their opening 10 Primeira Liga fixtures (D1, L7).

Both victories have come at Estadio da Madeira, offering some encouragement ahead of Saturday's encounter, knowing that taking maximum points at the weekend could hinge on defensive solidity, given their successes this term only came in games they kept clean sheets.

Supporters of the Alvinegros can also take some comfort from their side's record against Viseu in Funchal, having won three of the previous five meetings between the clubs (D1, L1) there, although their most recent home encounter ended in a 1-1 draw in Liga 2 in March 2024.

Viseu, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive start to life back in the top flight after failing to win any of their opening four fixtures, although an encouraging draw away to Benfica on matchday one offered an early indication of their potential.

Bruno Pinheiro's side have since recorded victories in each of their last six league matches, beating Gil Vicente, Vitoria de Guimaraes, Estrela Amadora, Estoril Praia and Sporting Lisbon before securing a 2-1 comeback triumph over Rio Ave last weekend.

That result means Academico have scored exactly twice in each of their last five top-flight outings, taking their league tally to 15 goals, with only the traditional big three of Porto (23), Benfica (27) and Sporting (23) finding the net more often.

Viseu have also alternated between league victories and cup defeats across their last four matches in all competitions, having been eliminated from the Taca de Portugal by lower-league Fatima before suffering Taca da Liga disappointment against Porto.

Pinheiro's men have also proved difficult to beat on the road, remaining one of only four sides yet to lose on their travels in the division, with three victories and two draws from five outings making them the league's fifth-best away team.

Academico de Viseu form (all competitions):

Nacional are expected to remain without long-term absentees Leo Santos, who is recovering from a knee injury, and Ulisses Rocha, who is sidelined with a broken ankle.

Brazilian duo Wesley Gasolina and Liziero, along with Filipe Soares, are all making progress in their respective recoveries, but Saturday's encounter is expected to come too soon for the trio.

Henriques could stick with a similar lineup to the one deployed in his first game in charge, with Abdel Njoya again expected to lead the attack as he looks to add to his two Primeira Liga goals this season.

Viseu are expected to have an almost clean bill of health for the trip to Madeira, although Igor Milioransa has not featured in a matchday squad since gameweek two and could miss out once again.

Andre Clovis provided the assist for Soufiane Messeguem's equaliser before scoring the winner against Rio Ave, and the striker will be keen to add to his five league goals when he leads the visitors' attack this weekend.

Marin; Jensen, Goncalves, Vitor, Kokolo; Goncalves, Dias, Baeza; Gavriel, Labidi, Njoya

Academico de Viseu possible starting lineup:

Ewerton; Robinho, Correia, Michelis, Brau; L Silva, Messeguem; Moreno, Kahraman, Guilherme; Clovis

Nacional will be desperate to turn their fortunes around and are expected to approach Saturday's encounter with that intention as Henriques seeks his first victory in charge, but the visitors' impressive winning run and unbeaten away record suggest they have enough to secure another three points.

Southampton will look to extend their six-game unbeaten run when they travel to Deepdale for Saturday’s clash with Preston North End.

The Saints are currently operating in seventh spot in the Championship standings, while PNE are propping up the table after taking just five points from their 14 matches.

Preston boss Graham Alexander has failed to spark an upturn in fortunes since being named as Paul Heckingbottom’s successor at the end of September.

Alexander has lost five of his six matches in charge (D1), including a 2-0 defeat in last Saturday’s away clash against Stoke City.

PNE experienced more disappointment in midweek, despite taking an early lead in their home meeting with Sheffield United.

Sydie Peck’s 19-minute hat-trick left Preston trailing by two goals at half time, and while Callum Lang pulled a goal back in the 77th minute, PNE ultimately failed to find an equaliser as they fell to their 11th Championship defeat of the season.

As a result of their struggles, Preston are already nine points adrift from safety, leaving them with a mountain to climb if they are to extend their 12-season stay in the second tier.

Alexander will be aware that his team needs to improve significantly in both boxes, as Preston currently have the league’s worst defensive record with 30 goals conceded and are among the division’s lowest scorers with just 12 goals to their name.

In contrast to their hosts, Southampton have proven to be a tough team to beat this term, having won eight, drawn four and lost just two of their 14 Championship matches.

They will certainly fancy their chances of adding three points to their tally against a struggling Preston side, especially as they have won on two of their previous three visits to Deepdale, including a 3-1 victory in May.

That said, they have struggled for consistency on their travels, having won two, drawn three and lost two of their seven away league games this season.

Preston are still having to contend without the services of Harry Clarke, Lewis Gibson, Liam Gibbs and Ali McCann.

Johnny Kenny has been added to the injury list after he was forced off in the 12th minute against Sheffield United due to a hamstring problem.

Midfielder Leo Leroy will miss Saturday’s game through suspension after collecting his fifth yellow card of the season in the midweek defeat.

As for the visitors, midfielder Caspar Jandar will have to be assessed after sitting out the last two games with a muscular injury.

Southampton’s top scorer Cyle Larin is another fitness concern, having been forced to miss the last three games with a hamstring problem.

Eckert, meanwhile, is confident Leo Scienza will be ready to feature at Deepdale after being ruled out for the midweek draw with West Brom.

With the Saints currently the league's third-highest scorers, we ultimately believe they will be too strong for a Preston side with the worst defensive record in the second tier.
