#1556. Angers vs Nice - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 06 Nov 2026 00:05

Angers can stay above the Ligue 1 relegation line on Sunday with a victory over a rejuvenated Nice at Stade Raymond Kopa.

A 2-0 defeat at Lyon last weekend dropped Les Scoistes down to 15th in the table, while Nice climbed up to eighth after a convincing 5-2 home win versus Rennes.

The fall international window seemed to kill any momentum Angers might have had leading up to that as they aim to get back in the win column this weekend for the first time since September.

Stephane Gilli’s men have claimed just one point from their last four Ligue 1 affairs since the season resumed in October, putting them a point above Le Mans who are currently in the last automatic relegation place.

This team have won just one of their five home games in the competition this season, going without a point in three of those outings.

So far in 2026-27 they have allowed nine goals at home in Ligue 1, one more than they gave up in their final eight league fixtures a season ago.

Defending dead-ball situations has been an issue for them this season, as they are tied with Auxerre for the second-most set-piece goals conceded (five) in the competition so far.

Les Scoistes have yet to earn a single point domestically against a Ligue 1 side currently in the top half of the table after nine matchdays.

It appears as though Olivier Pantaloni has at last been able to get Nice on track, with his team showing plenty of consistency since the fall.

The club, who were a game away from relegation a season ago, have won four of their last five league fixtures, and could win three straight top flight outings this weekend for the first time in 2026.

Le Gym can also claim their second away triumph of the campaign, which would match their total from the 2026 portion of last season.

Nice have lost their only domestic away match of the campaign when netting first, with their lone triumph as the visitors occurring after conceding the opener.

After nine Ligue 1 matchdays, they have amassed the same number of points that they had at this stage of last season (14).

The side from southern France  are unbeaten versus Angers at Stade Raymond Kopa this decade, winning four of those six outings.

A calf strain will likely prevent Oumar Pona from featuring for Angers, though, Anthony Lopes likely would have gotten the call between the sticks regardless.

Amine El Ouazzini is expected to sit out as well, with Haris Belkebla and Prosper Peter likely to be the attacking pair.

At Nice, Laurent Abergel and Antoine Mendy are recovering from cruciate ligament tears, Moise Bombito remains doubtful with a lower leg fracture, Ali Abdi has a leg issue, while Axel Witsel is questionable because of a muscle strain.

Elye Wahi netted a hat-trick for them against Rennes, with Jonathan Clauss and Mohamed Amoura also scoring at Allianz Riviera.

Lopes; Raolisoa, Arcus, Camara, Lefort, Kalulu; Belkhdim, Van den Boomen, Allevinah; Peter, Belkebla

Diouf; Mandza, Ndayishimiye, Abdelmonem; Clauss, Coulibaly, Boudaoui, Nkounkou; Diop, Hein; Wahi

Nice are starting to find their form and given how strong they are in possession we expect they will eventually wear down the home side and come out on top.

#1555. Wily veterans and the fountain of youth: The five key battles in Milan vs. Ferencvaros

AC Milan return to Europa League action at San Siro this evening for a must-win game against high-flyers Ferencvaros.

Starting their European campaign with two defeats (vs. Benfica and Bournemouth) and one win last left Milan down in 24th in the table, meaning that they need to turn things around if they are to mount a surge towards the top eight spots.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tonight’s game will be far from straightforward though, as Ferencvaros have taken nine points from nine and therefore sit fourth in the table. They are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and are two points from the summit in their domestic league, with a game in hand to play.

Reports are suggesting that Ruben Amorim will turn to a youthful line-up for this one despite the status of being a must-win game. However, the spine of the team will still be made up of players who must deliver.

Starting with a rather unconventional battle, the one between the two goalkeepers Lorenzo Torriani and Dénes Dibusz could be potentially decisive, for obvious reasons. Ferencvaros have conceded just three goals in their three Europa games so far and just 10 in 10 in the league, and the 35-year-old veteran Dibusz has been a big part of that, even if there has been some rotation.

For Torriani, this is arguably his biggest opportunity in a Milan shirt. His only other start came in a Coppa Italia rout of Sassuolo, while he came off the bench in a Champions League defeat to Liverpool, and in the Bournemouth defeat. This is a huge chance for the 20-year-old to not only show he is a capable deputy in the present, but a potential Mike Maignan successor down the line.

There will also be two crucial duels involving the two Nagys, Oliver and Adam. The former will play at right-back and faces the difficult task of keeping Alphadjo Cisse quiet. The Italian is the Rossoneri’s top scorer this season and will be champing at the bit to build on his hat-trick against RB Salzburg. Oliver Nagy is dangerous going forward though, with two assists in his five starts, so Cisse will have to help out defensively too.

Adam Nagy meanwhile faces the task of stopping Milan’s second-top scorer, Adrien Rabiot. The Frenchman netted his fifth of the season in the derby against Inter, and Amorim has chosen to rely on his experience against an opponent who is also 31 years of age. The Hungarian signed from Spezia in the summer and is best known for his appearances at the 2016, 2020 and 2024 UEFA European Championships for his national team.

Ferencvaros have two main threats that Milan must keep quiet, especially the way that this game could play out with the visitors no doubt keen to contain and counter. Bamidele Yusuf is the first, and the Nigerian is expected to start up front this evening though he can also play and drift wide. He has six goals and three assists in 10 starts this season for the green and whites.

Bamidele Yusuf 🎯#UEL | @Fradi_HU pic.twitter.com/AXnt4XPaSu

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) October 29, 2026

Sanhoun Diawara will have to do his bit to keep Yusuf quiet, but our feeling is that Koni De Winter will take on the man-marking duties just like he did with Inter’s lone striker Marcus Thuram in the derby. The Belgian has been undroppable in a literal sense, so we hope that no signs of fatigue are seen especially in transition, like against Bologna.

The visitors’ other danger man is Kristoffer Zachariassen, who matches Yusuf on nine goal contributions (seven goals, two assists) for the season. The 32-year-old Norwegian has plenty of experience and an eye for goal from the attacking midfield role, though his heat maps show he tends to drift to the right too.

So, it will be down to Ardon Jashari to keep tabs on him. Amorim and Milan are still waiting for the Swiss to put together a good run of solid starts after his arrival from Club Brugge for over €30m, and this is the kind of game that he needs to seize control of and dominate to show he is capable of being the anchor man, especially with Luka Modric’s retirement surely not far away.

#1554. Lazio’s Turin win leaves Juventus eight points off Serie A lead

Juventus lost 3-0 at home to Lazio on Sunday, October 18, as goals from Oliver Provstgaard, Gustav Isaksen and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru kept the visitors level with Inter at the top of Serie A. The result, reported by Football Italia and confirmed in Juventus’ match report, was Lazio’s first league victory in Turin since October 2017.

Lazio took the lead in the 37th minute after a short corner, with Mattia Zaccagni’s delivery finding Provstgaard for a glancing header from close range. Isaksen made it 2-0 in the 66th, controlling Nuno Tavares’ cross-field pass before cutting inside and finding the far bottom corner.

Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, carrying the ball forward from inside his own half before beating Guglielmo Vicario with an angled drive. Juventus had chances to respond: Randal Kolo Muani had an effort ruled out for offside, while Nick Woltemade and Nico Gonzalez both went close. The match statistics showed 58 per cent possession for the hosts and nine shots apiece, but Lazio registered three efforts on target to Juventus’ two.

The loss came after a demanding week. Juventus had beaten Celta Vigo 2-1 away in the Europa League on Thursday, but had managed only one win in their previous four league rounds. Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Jeff Ekhator and Kamil Grabara were unavailable, while Jeremie Boga returned to the bench. Luciano Spalletti served a touchline ban following his altercation with Cagliari coach Fabio Pisacane, leaving assistant Marco Domenichini in charge from the bench.

Lazio needed the win to remain joint leaders, and the result left the Bianconeri with more ground to make up. According to Corriere della Sera, Juventus sit eighth on 11 points, eight behind Inter and Lazio, who have 19 each. The defeat adds to the concern around a season in which Juventus have struggled to turn performances into league results, following their draw with Cagliari.

Corriere also reports Juventus have a goal difference of +1, compared with +12 for Inter and +10 for Lazio. The standings sharpen the pressure on Juventus to respond in the next league rounds, while Lazio leave Turin with a sizeable result and their place alongside Inter at the summit intact.
